"description": "Flat cross-domain fault registry for ComLab. v0.1 ships with the three starter rules from OrchestratorLabBP.md plus a synthetic catalyst-efficiency rule. New faults are added by appending to this array \u2014 no Python changes required.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Three-way catalyst oxygen storage capacity depleted below the OBD monitor threshold \u2014 post-cat O2 switching ratio approaching 1:1.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Catalyst ceramic substrate melted and collapsed from sustained misfire dumping raw fuel \u2014 housing shows heat discolouration and backpressure exceeds 3.0 psi at 2500 RPM.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Exhaust flow restricted by partially collapsed substrate or carbon-clogged honeycomb \u2014 CO2 collapses under load as volumetric efficiency drops.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Catalyst has lost all conversion \u2014 oxidation and reduction both failed. Tailpipe HC exceeds 250 ppm with-cat, CO above 1.5 %, CO2 below 13 %, post-cat O2 flat at reference voltage.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Healthy catalyst oxidising rich feed-gas \u2014 clean tailpipe masks a serious upstream rich condition. Strongly negative LTFT is the tell.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Catalyst washcoat poisoned by phosphorus and zinc from engine oil consumption \u2014 glassy coating permanently blocks OSC sites, gradual P0420 onset.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Catalyst has not reached light-off temperature (> 250 \u00b0C) \u2014 CO/HC oxidation and NOx reduction stalled. Check O2 heater circuit, thermostat, or short-trip operating pattern.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Exhaust manifold-to-head gasket failure allowing atmospheric air into the exhaust stream \u2014 upstream O2 sensor reads false-lean, driving positive fuel trim correction.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Cracked exhaust manifold (cast iron or tubular) admitting air pre-O2 sensor \u2014 pulse-synchronous false-lean O2 reading with audible cold-engine ticking.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Bolted flange leak at manifold-to-downpipe joint \u2014 false-lean if O2 sensor is downstream of the leak; noise without trim disturbance if O2 is upstream.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Flex pipe bellows ruptured post-catalyst \u2014 no O2 sensor or trim impact; primary symptoms are exhaust noise and possible cabin fume entry.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "EGR feed tube crack or pinhole leak \u2014 exhaust gas escapes before reaching EGR valve, reducing actual EGR flow; false-lean if leak is pre-O2 sensor.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Compression donut gasket at exhaust slip-joint or spring-bolted flange has deteriorated \u2014 exhaust leak under load with no trim disturbance unless pre-O2.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "ECU ignition coil driver transistor failing \u2014 coil fires intermittently or not at all; misfire stays on the cylinder after coil swap, confirming the fault is upstream in the ECU.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Worn ignition switch contacts causing voltage drop in coil primary supply \u2014 coil primary voltage below 10.5 V during cranking produces weak or absent spark.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "CKP sensor signal dropping out intermittently \u2014 ECU loses crankshaft position reference, causing random no-spark events registered as P0300 random misfire.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Head gasket fire ring breached between two adjacent cylinders \u2014 combustion pressure crosses the gasket land during compression and power strokes. Two adjacent cylinders read 30-60 psi below bank average on compression test.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Head gasket breached between combustion chamber and coolant passage \u2014 combustion gas forced into cooling system during power stroke. Continuous bubbles in radiator at idle confirm the leak path.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Piston rings worn beyond specification \u2014 compression ring face barrel profile lost, oil control ring drain-back holes carbon-plugged. Wet compression test positive (>= 20 psi rise). Continuous oil burning and crankcase blow-by.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Valve stem seals hardened, cracked, or worn \u2014 lip seal no longer wipes oil from valve stem. Blue-white smoke puff at cold start (clears in 2-5 seconds) and on snap-throttle. Compression typically normal because rings seal pressure.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Uniformly low compression across all or most cylinders (60-80 psi) from high-mileage ring/cylinder wear or jumped timing. Vacuum gauge steady but abnormally low at 10-15 inHg. Engine idles rough, lacks power under load.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Single cylinder bore scored \u2014 vertical gouges from debris ingestion, detonation, or oil starvation. Affected cylinder 30-50 psi below bank average with minimal wet-test recovery (< 10 psi rise). Oil-fouled plug on that cylinder only.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Timing chain stretched beyond tensioner range or belt jumped one tooth \u2014 cam phasing globally retarded. All cylinders equally low compression. Classic wrong-valve-timing gas fingerprint: very high HC (> 1000 ppm) plus elevated O2 (> 5 %).",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "VVT phaser locked in full-advance position \u2014 internal lock pin seized or spool valve jammed. Intake valves open too early causing knock under light load and rough/loping idle from exhaust reversion. P0011/P0021 DTCs set.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "VVT phaser locked in full-retard position \u2014 lock pin seized or debris overrides return spring. Engine flat and gutless below 3500 RPM, wakes up above 4000 RPM. HC 1000-3000 ppm with mild rich lambda. P0014/P0024 DTCs set.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "VVT phaser responds sluggishly to ECU commands \u2014 oil sludge/varnish obstructing solenoid screen and phaser oil galleries. Phaser lags commanded angle by 0.5-2.0 seconds. Transient hesitation during throttle changes. Often sets no DTC.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "VVT oil control solenoid electrically degraded \u2014 coil resistance drifted beyond 6-14 ohm spec, internal spool valve stuck, or connector pin corrosion. ECU cannot position phaser. P0010/P0020 circuit DTCs set.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Weak spark or marginal fuel delivery \u2014 intermittent firing during cranking never sustains. HC moderate (200-800 ppm), CO2 depressed (3-6 %), O2 high (12-18 %), lambda lean (1.20-1.50).",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Unmetered air entering the intake downstream of the MAF sensor \u2014 vacuum leak causing true lean combustion with idle-dominant positive fuel trim correction.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Fuel pump unable to maintain rail pressure under demand \u2014 stress-RPM-dominant lean from fuel starvation. Fuel pressure drops under load.",
"ui_diagnostic_string": "Partially blocked fuel injector nozzle \u2014 cylinder-specific or bank-specific lean from restricted fuel flow. May show bank-asymmetric trim on dual-bank engines.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Severely clogged fuel injector causing cylinder lean misfire \u2014 restricted flow below reliable ignition threshold. Misfire DTC with lean fuel trim confirms injector-level restriction.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Worn valve stem seals drawing engine oil into the combustion chamber on valve open \u2014 idle-dominant oil burn produces elevated HC with POA-style chemistry. Replace all valve stem seals as a set; inspect guides for clearance.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Worn piston rings allow oil blow-by on both compression and intake strokes \u2014 POA chemistry with HC elevated at both idle and high-idle. Confirm with wet compression test; bottom-end rebuild required.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Fuel injector pintle not sealing \u2014 drip leak into the manifold delivering excess fuel. Strong negative trim with rich chemistry and no mechanical symptom. Perform injector pressure-drop balance test; replace leaking injector.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "EVAP purge solenoid stuck open dumping raw fuel vapour from the charcoal canister into the intake \u2014 rich chemistry with very high HC. Replace the purge control valve; verify canister is free of liquid fuel.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Engine coolant temperature sensor biased cold \u2014 ECU locked in cold-start enrichment after warm-up, forcing rich chemistry. Compare ECT PID against mechanical thermostat temperature; replace drifted ECT sensor.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Vacuum-referenced fuel pressure regulator diaphragm ruptured \u2014 fuel leaking through the vacuum reference line into the intake manifold. Strong rich condition with raw fuel deposits on vacuum line. Replace mechanical FPR.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Carbon or oil deposits bridging spark plug electrode gap \u2014 conductive shunt bleeds ignition energy causing intermittent misfire. Remove and inspect plugs; if fouled black, investigate root cause (rich running or oil consumption).",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Electrode metal erosion widens spark plug gap beyond coil secondary voltage capability \u2014 lean-type misfires dominant at idle where coil dwell time is shortest. Measure gap; replace all plugs if gap > 0.2 mm over OEM spec.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Open or shorted primary winding prevents ECM from energising coil \u2014 cylinder completely dead with every cycle misfiring. Severe IGNITION_MISFIRE with extreme positive trim. Measure primary resistance (0.5-2.0 ohm); swap coil to confirm; replace failed coil.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Open circuit in fuel injector solenoid \u2014 no fuel to affected cylinder. Air-only cylinder produces LEAN_MISFIRE with bank-specific positive trim spike. Simultaneous P020X injector circuit + P030X misfire DTC on same cylinder is the strongest combined signal.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Severe compression loss from ring, valve, or bore degradation \u2014 misfire persists after ignition and fuel systems ruled out. Perform wet/dry compression test and leak-down test to pinpoint leak location. Mechanical repair required \u2014 no ignition or fuel system fix will resolve.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Carbon deposits accumulate on GDI intake valves due to absent port fuel washing \u2014 restricts intake flow and disrupts charge motion causing lean misfire at idle and part-load. Borescope intake ports to confirm; walnut blast media clean to remove deposits.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Spark plug carbon fouling from rich-mixture misfire \u2014 excess fuel washing down cylinder walls and depositing conductive carbon on plug insulator. Black matte or oily black deposits across electrode and insulator nose.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "VVT phaser locked in full-retard position \u2014 lock pin seized or debris overrides return spring. Engine flat and gutless below 3500 RPM, wakes up above 4000 RPM. HC 1000-3000 ppm with mild rich lambda. P0014/P0024 DTCs set.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Upstream O2 sensor element is dead \u2014 output voltage is fixed (stuck rich > 0.7 V or stuck lean < 0.2 V) with no switching. Circuit DTC (P0131/P0132/P0134) confirms electrical failure. Gas analyser lambda_chem may be near-normal while ECU perception is pegged.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Upstream O2 sensor responding sluggishly \u2014 ECU over-corrects fuel trim because delayed feedback causes oscillation. Gas analyser lambda_chem is near-stoichiometric ground truth but OBD lambda perception is biased high (sensor reads falsely lean). No circuit DTC \u2014 sensor still switches, just too slowly.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Upstream O2 sensor responding sluggishly \u2014 ECU under-fuels because delayed feedback causes oscillation. Gas analyser lambda_chem is near-stoichiometric ground truth but OBD lambda perception is biased low (sensor reads falsely rich). No circuit DTC \u2014 sensor still switches, just too slowly.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "ECM internal processor/memory self-test failure (P0606). The ECU is reporting that it is defective \u2014 all ECU-reported sensor values become unreliable. Gas analyser is the sole ground-truth data source.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Invalid gas sample (CO+CO2+O2 outside 14-18% window) masking a cam-timing fault. Probe leak, analyser fault, or exhaust-sample contamination producing unclassifiable chemistry. Re-test with verified sampling equipment.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Oil-burning chemistry (POA_SIGNATURE) with lean-condition symptoms. Oil consumption causing both rich-perceived O2 displacement AND actual lean-running from PCV unmetered air or ring-blowby dilution of intake charge. Check PCV system integrity and perform leak-down test.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Invalid gas sample (sum-of-gases outside 14-18%) with lean-condition symptoms. Unreliable chemistry masking the true air-fuel ratio. Resolve the sampling fault (probe leak, analyser calibration, exhaust leak) and re-test before diagnosing lean condition.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Incomplete-combustion gas chemistry with rich-mixture symptoms. Partial burn from ignition weakness producing elevated HC with depressed CO2, reading as rich on a non-lambda analyser. Check spark-plug condition, coil output, and ignition timing before diagnosing fuel delivery.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Normal gas chemistry with sensor-fault symptoms. The engine is running correctly but a sensor is reporting implausible values to the ECU. The gas analyser shows normal combustion while OBD data shows a sensor fault. Check O2 sensor, MAF/MAP, ECT, and IAT sensor plausibility against known-good values.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Ignition coil secondary winding breakdown under heat soak. Spark energy collapses when coil reaches operating temperature, producing raw-fuel misfire with elevated HC and O2. Engine may start cold and stall hot. Swap coil to confirm; misfire follows the coil.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Weak or marginal spark producing incomplete combustion. Coil primary voltage supply compromised by corroded relay contacts, failing ignition switch, or high-resistance ground. HC moderately elevated (300-800 ppm), CO depressed, CO2 below 10%, O2 elevated from partial burn. Check coil supply voltage during cranking and running.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Complete ignition system failure \u2014 no spark on any cylinder. Engine cranks but produces zero combustion, so gas analyser reads ambient air (no valid exhaust sample). Confirm no-spark with adjustable spark tester at 20 mm gap. Check CKP sensor signal, ignition relay, and ECU power supply before condemning coils.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Ignition coil primary or secondary failure preventing spark generation. Engine cranks with normal RPM but zero combustion \u2014 gas analyser shows ambient air. Confirm cranking RPM is normal via PID, disable fuel pump, crank and verify no spark with spark tester. Replace failed coil(s). If ECU driver failed, repair or replace ECU.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Marginal spark energy allows intermittent firing during cranking but never sustains combustion. HC moderate (200-800 ppm), CO2 depressed (3-6%), O2 high (12-18%), lambda lean (1.20-1.50). Check battery voltage during cranking, coil primary supply, and spark-plug condition. Weak spark often from low cranking voltage or coil degradation.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Fuel delivery failure preventing start \u2014 no fuel pressure at the rail despite normal cranking. Gas analyser shows lean mixture (lambda > 1.20, HC low, CO near zero) from fuel starvation. Check fuel-pump relay, pump operation, and fuel pressure at the rail during cranking. KOEO pressure must reach specification within 2 seconds.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Pre-O2 exhaust leak causing false-lean O2 reading that drives the ECU to over-fuel, producing incomplete-combustion chemistry with elevated HC and depressed CO2. The analyser sees raw fuel + diluted O2 as a partial-burn signature. Confirm leak with smoke test or cold-engine listening; the chemistry normalises when the leak is sealed.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Severe exhaust leak contaminating the tailpipe sample with ambient air. Sum-of-gases check fails (CO+CO2+O2 outside 14-18% window) because the analyser is sampling diluted exhaust. Verify sampling probe seal and exhaust system integrity. Fix the leak and re-test before diagnosing engine condition.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Oil-burning chemistry (POA_SIGNATURE: HC normal-high, CO low, lambda ~1) from mechanical engine wear. Worn piston rings, valve guides, or valve stem seals allowing oil into the combustion chamber. Consistent oil consumption with blue-white exhaust smoke. Perform wet/dry compression test and leak-down to isolate the leak path.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Compression-loss misfire from mechanical wear producing an ignition-misfire gas signature. Low compression prevents proper combustion, reads as unburned fuel + O2 spike indistinguishable from ignition failure on gas alone. Perform compression test to confirm mechanical basis. Wet test rise > 20 psi confirms ring wear; no rise points to valves or head gasket.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "ECU sensor-ground offset or 5V reference drift causing systematic lean bias in fuel control. The ECU perceives a richer mixture than actual, pulling fuel trim negative until the engine runs truly lean. Gas analyser confirms lean combustion while ECU data shows negative fuel trim. Verify ECU grounds and sensor reference voltages against specification.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "ECU injector-driver leakage or MAP sensor 5V-reference over-voltage causing systematic rich bias. The ECU perceives a leaner mixture than actual, adding fuel until the engine runs truly rich. Gas analyser confirms rich chemistry while ECU data shows positive fuel trim. Scope injector waveforms for stuck-on events; verify MAP sensor calibration.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Retarded ignition or cam timing causing lean-perceived gas chemistry. Late combustion reduces effective cylinder pressure and temperature, producing elevated O2 with depressed CO2 that mimics a lean mixture. Verify base ignition timing and cam/crank correlation at TDC. A jumped timing belt or stretched chain retards cam timing globally.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Ignition misfire producing a lean-appearing gas signature from unburned oxygen passing through to the tailpipe. The O2 sensor and gas analyser both see elevated O2, but the root cause is ignition failure, not excess air. Rule out ignition (plugs, coils, CKP signal) before diagnosing a fuel-delivery or air-induction fault.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Ignition misfire producing a rich-perceived gas signature. Raw unburned fuel from a dead cylinder passes directly to the exhaust, elevating HC dramatically (1000+ ppm) and depressing O2 \u2014 the analyser reads this as a rich mixture. Confirm ignition first (swap coil, inspect plug) before condemning the fuel system.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Sensor fault producing lean-mixture chemistry through ECU mis-fueling. MAF sensor under-reading (dirty hot-wire), MAP sensor vacuum leak at the sensor port, or IAT sensor reading hot \u2014 all cause the ECU to under-fuel, creating true lean combustion. Compare sensor readings against known-good references; clean or replace drifted sensors.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Sensor fault producing rich-mixture chemistry through ECU mis-fueling. ECT sensor biased cold (stuck at low resistance), MAF over-reading (oil contamination), or fuel-rail pressure sensor reading high \u2014 all cause the ECU to over-fuel, creating true rich combustion. Compare ECT against mechanical thermostat temperature; clean MAF hot-wire; verify fuel pressure with mechanical gauge.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Timing chain stretch or belt elongation causing globally retarded cam timing. All cylinders show low compression, vacuum gauge reads steady but low (10-15 inHg), and gas analyser shows timing-retarded chemistry (high HC, elevated O2). Verify cam timing mechanically at TDC with timing marks aligned. Replace timing chain/belt, tensioner, and guides as a complete kit.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Severe cam/crank misalignment causing incomplete-combustion gas chemistry. When valve timing is far enough off, combustion becomes so inefficient that it reads as partial burn \u2014 HC very high, CO2 depressed below 10%, O2 elevated. Verify cam timing mechanically at TDC. A jumped belt or chain is the likely cause; inspect tensioner and guides for failure.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Intermittent misfire not active during the diagnostic session. Engine runs smoothly at time of test, but patient reports random hesitation, rough idle when cold, or MIL flashing under load. Review Mode 06 misfire counts per cylinder. Inspect spark plugs for gap erosion, coils for heat-related degradation, and injectors for intermittent sticking.",

"ui_diagnostic_string": "Rich-mixture misfire without active MIL. Carbon-fouled spark plug from persistent rich running causes intermittent misfire that has not yet tripped the OBD misfire monitor (Mode 06 counts below the P0300 threshold). Black matte deposits on plug insulator. Correct the rich condition first, then replace fouled plugs. Verify misfire counts return to zero.",

"catalyst_efficiency_below_threshold": "Rule out feed-gas faults (misfire, fuel trim, exhaust leak) before condemning the catalyst. Check Mode $06 catalyst monitor data and IR temperature delta. Replace catalytic converter if OSC is confirmed depleted.",

"catalyst_substrate_meltdown": "Identify and repair the root cause that dumped fuel into the catalyst (misfire, leaking injector) before replacing the converter. Replace catalytic converter and both O2 sensors. Inspect exhaust manifold and downstream components for heat damage.",

"catalyst_flow_restriction": "Perform backpressure test at idle and 2500 RPM. Inspect substrate face with borescope for soot or collapse. Replace catalytic converter if backpressure remains above 3.0 psi at 2500 RPM.",

"dead_catalyst_hc_nox_breakthrough": "Confirm dead cat with tailpipe gas analyser \u2014 compare pre-cat vs post-cat emissions. Check for poisoning source before replacement. Replace catalytic converter and post-cat O2 sensor.",

"catalyst_masking_rich_engine": "Do NOT replace the catalyst \u2014 it is healthy. Chase the upstream rich condition: check fuel pressure, injector leak-down, EVAP purge function, and HPFP seal (GDI). Fix the root cause; the cat will recover once the rich feed-gas stops.",

"catalyst_oil_poisoning": "Identify and repair the oil consumption root cause (valve seals, piston rings, PCV) before replacing the converter \u2014 a new cat will be poisoned within weeks if the oil path is not closed. Replace catalytic converter; poisoned washcoat cannot be regenerated.",

"catalyst_below_lightoff_temperature": "Check pre-cat O2 sensor heater circuit resistance and thermostat opening temperature. For short-trip-only vehicles, document as operating pattern. Replace failed O2 sensor or thermostat. Verify catalyst reaches > 250 \u00b0C within 5 minutes of cold start.",

"exhaust_manifold_gasket_leak": "Confirm exhaust leak with cold-engine listening test and exhaust analyser probe at the manifold-to-head joint. Replace the failed exhaust manifold gasket. Inspect manifold flange for flatness \u2014 a warped flange will cause the new gasket to fail.",

"ignition_coil_driver_fault": "Swap suspect coil with known-good cylinder \u2014 if misfire stays on original cylinder, the fault is upstream. Back-probe coil primary control wire with lab scope. Replace or repair ECU if driver transistor is confirmed failed.",

"ignition_switch_voltage_drop": "Measure coil primary supply voltage during cranking \u2014 below 10.5 V confirms supply-side drop. Perform voltage-drop test across ignition switch. Replace ignition switch if drop exceeds 0.3 V.",

"head_gasket_coolant_passage_leak": "Perform block test to confirm combustion gas in coolant. Remove cylinder head. Replace head gasket. Flush cooling system thoroughly. Change engine oil \u2014 coolant contamination destroys bearing protection.",

"worn_piston_rings": "Confirm with wet compression test (>= 20 psi rise). Engine requires bottom-end rebuild: piston rings, cylinder hone or bore, possibly pistons. Inspect PCV system before teardown. This is a major mechanical repair.",

"worn_valve_stem_seals": "Replace all valve stem seals as a set (intake and exhaust). Inspect valve guides for excessive clearance while seals are off \u2014 worn guides will destroy new seals. Verify: no blue smoke on cold start or snap-throttle.",

"low_compression_multi_cylinder": "Check cam timing first \u2014 if timing marks align and wet test raises compression, rings are the cause. If timing is correct and rings confirmed worn: full engine rebuild (rings, hone, possibly oversize pistons, bearings). Engine-out major repair.",

"vvt_phaser_stuck_advanced": "Check engine oil condition first \u2014 flush if sludged. Replace VVT phaser, oil control solenoid, and all O-rings and gaskets. Flush engine oil system to remove debris. Verify: no knock under light load, P0011/P0021 does not return.",

"vvt_phaser_stuck_retarded": "Check engine oil condition first \u2014 flush if sludged. Replace VVT phaser, oil control solenoid, and all seals. Flush engine oil system thoroughly. Verify: power delivery smooth from 1500 RPM to redline, P0014/P0024 does not return.",

"vvt_solenoid_fault": "Measure solenoid coil resistance (typically 6-14 ohm at 20 C). Inspect spool valve screen for debris. Apply 12 V to verify spool valve clicks. Replace VVT solenoid if confirmed faulty. Use OEM-quality replacement.",

"no_spark_coil_failure": "Confirm cranking RPM is normal (150-300 via PID $0C) to rule out CKP failure. Disable fuel pump (pull fuse), crank, and verify no spark on any cylinder with spark tester. Replace failed ignition coil(s). If ECU driver is confirmed failed, repair or replace ECU.",

"rich_no_start_ect_sensor": "Read ECT PID: -40 C on warm engine = open circuit. Attempt WOT clear-flood \u2014 if engine fires, flooding is confirmed. Measure ECT sensor resistance and compare to manufacturer spec. Replace failed ECT sensor. Verify cold-start enrichment tapers to stoichiometric within 30 seconds.",

"no_fuel_delivery": "Check cranking RPM PID first \u2014 0 RPM routes to CKP failure. KOEO fuel pressure test: must reach spec within 2 seconds. Noid light test for injector pulse during cranking. Check immobiliser security light. Replace fuel pump if confirmed dead. If injector circuit fault, diagnose wiring before replacing injectors.",

"lean_no_start_weak_spark": "Check battery voltage during cranking \u2014 below 10.0 V starves coils and injectors. Inspect spark plugs for fouling, carbon tracking, or gap erosion. Test coil secondary with adjustable spark tester \u2014 spark must jump 20 mm gap. Verify fuel pressure holds during extended cranking. If all pass, perform relative compression test.",

"ckp_sensor_failure_no_rpm": "Read RPM PID during cranking \u2014 zero RPM with audible cranking confirms CKP failure. Scan for P0335/P0336. Inspect CKP connector and harness for corrosion or chafing. Measure CKP sensor resistance (200-1000 ohm typical for inductive). Replace CKP sensor and perform CASE relearn if required.",

"spark_plug_carbon_fouled": "Remove all spark plugs and inspect \u2014 carbon-fouled plug shows black matte or oily black deposits across electrode and insulator nose. Identify the fouled plug(s). Replace all fouled spark plugs with OEM-specified plugs. Investigate and repair the root cause of fouling (rich running or oil consumption) before replacing plugs.",

"spark_plug_gap_erosion": "Remove and measure spark plug gap with feeler gauge \u2014 gap more than 0.2 mm above OEM spec confirms erosion. Replace all spark plugs simultaneously. Verify: misfire DTCs clear and HC returns to < 100 ppm after one drive cycle.",

"ignition_coil_primary_winding_failure": "Measure primary winding resistance with multimeter (typically 0.5-2.0 ohm). Open circuit or short confirms failure. Swap suspect coil to known-good cylinder. Replace failed coil. Check ECM coil driver if repeated coil failures occur.",

"dead_injector_cylinder_misfire": "Measure injector solenoid resistance (typically 12-16 ohm). Open circuit or short confirms failure. Use noid light to verify ECM pulse signal. Replace dead injector. Verify: cylinder contribution test shows HC response when cylinder is disabled.",

"low_compression_mechanical_misfire": "Perform dry compression test on all cylinders \u2014 any below 80% OEM spec or 689 kPa (100 psi) confirms. Perform wet test: if compression rises, ring seal is cause; if unchanged, valve seating is cause. Perform leak-down test to confirm and locate leak. Mechanical repair required.",

"gdi_intake_valve_carbon_buildup": "Perform borescope inspection of intake ports and valve heads \u2014 heavy black carbon deposits confirm diagnosis. Perform walnut shell media blasting through intake ports with intake valves closed. Consider adding catch can to crankcase breather circuit. Document cleaning interval (60 000-100 000 km on GDI platforms).",

"upstream_o2_sensor_lazy_response": "Observe upstream O2 sensor switching frequency on a scan tool \u2014 healthy sensor switches > 0.5 Hz at warm idle; lazy sensor < 0.25 Hz. Check O2 heater circuit resistance. Note: gas analyser lambda_chem is ground truth \u2014 if near 1.0 but sensor signal is not switching normally, sensor is suspect. Replace the upstream O2 sensor and verify switching frequency returns to > 0.5 Hz.",

"upstream_o2_sensor_fixed_voltage": "Observe upstream O2 sensor voltage in scan tool live data \u2014 stuck-rich > 0.7 V indefinitely; stuck-lean < 0.2 V indefinitely. Verify with gas analyser: if lambda_chem is normal but sensor reads stuck, sensor is confirmed dead. Check O2 heater circuit resistance. Replace the upstream O2 sensor. After replacement, verify sensor begins switching within 30 seconds of engine start."
"description": "JSON Schema for one kg/<family>.json file. Mirrors comlab.schemas.kg.KGFile. Source: COMLab_LLD.md §3.4.",
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Timing Chain/Belt and Camshaft Phasing Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Timing chain stretched beyond tensioner range or belt jumped one tooth. Cam phasing globally retarded \u2014 intake valves open/close later than designed. All cylinders equally low compression.",
"Compression test all cylinders: uniformly low across the board (60-80 psi where 120-180 psi is expected). Wet test on a representative cylinder: little or no change \u2014 rings are not the cause.",

"Verify cam timing mechanically: rotate engine to TDC compression stroke on cylinder 1. Check camshaft timing mark aligns with crank timing mark. A misalignment of one tooth or more confirms the timing has jumped.",
"Vacuum gauge at warm idle: steady but abnormally low (10-15 inHg). Engine idles rough and lacks power under load. Snap-throttle: vacuum plunges sluggishly and fails to rebound above baseline.",
"Verify repair: compression restored to 120-180 psi across all cylinders, vacuum gauge steady 17-22 inHg at warm idle, engine idles smoothly, power restored. Perform CASE relearn if required."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Variable Valve Timing (VVT) Phaser and Oil Control Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "VVT phaser locked full-advance \u2014 lock pin seized, spool valve jammed, or return spring broken. Intake valves open too early, raising low-RPM cylinder pressure causing knock under light load. Rough/loping idle from exhaust reversion into intake port.",
"Scan for DTCs: P0011 (intake cam over-advanced, bank 1) or P0021 (bank 2) confirm ECU has detected phaser stuck beyond commanded position. Check freeze-frame for actual vs desired cam angle delta.",
"Road test: light-throttle acceleration from ~1500 RPM produces audible knock (pinging) that diminishes at higher RPM \u2014 advanced cam timing creates excessive low-RPM cylinder pressure.",
"Verify repair: no knock/pinging under light load, P0011/P0021 does not return, actual cam angle tracks desired angle within 2 degrees, engine idles smoothly."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Variable Valve Timing (VVT) Phaser and Oil Control Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "VVT phaser locked full-retard \u2014 lock pin seized, spool valve jammed, or debris overrides return spring. Intake valves open/close late, reducing compression and cylinder fill at low-to-mid RPM. Engine flat below 3500 RPM.",
"Scan for DTCs: P0014 (intake cam over-retarded, bank 1) or P0024 (bank 2). If no DTC but engine feels weak at low RPM, phaser may be stuck without exceeding ECU detection threshold.",

"Road test: engine feels flat and unresponsive below 3000-3500 RPM. Above 4000 RPM it wakes up because cam retard becomes beneficial. This RPM-dependent power delivery is a strong VVT-phaser-stuck signal.",
"Check engine oil condition and level first \u2014 dirty or low oil is the most common cause. Perform oil change with correct viscosity before further diagnosis.",

"Bi-directional scan tool: command VVT phaser from full retard to full advance at warm idle. If actual cam angle does not move, phaser or solenoid is stuck. If it moves sluggishly, suspect sludge (see ERR-CT-004).",
"If phaser confirmed stuck retarded: replace VVT phaser, oil control solenoid, and all seals. Flush engine oil system thoroughly \u2014 sludge that killed old phaser will kill the new one.",
"Verify repair: power delivery smooth from 1500 RPM to redline, no flat spot, P0014/P0024 does not return, actual cam angle tracks desired within 2 degrees, HC returns to normal range."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Variable Valve Timing (VVT) Oil Supply and Phaser Response",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Sludge/varnish obstructs VVT solenoid screen and phaser oil galleries. Phaser moves but lags commanded angle 0.5-2.0 s. Transient lean/rich during throttle changes. Often no DTC \u2014 phaser eventually reaches target; fault is response time, not final position.",

"Scan tool: graph actual vs desired cam angle during throttle snap at warm idle. Healthy phaser tracks within 0.2 seconds. Sludge lag shows actual trace visibly chasing desired trace with 0.5-2.0 second delay.",
"Road test: light-throttle acceleration from 1500-2500 RPM produces momentary hesitation \u2014 phaser is still moving to commanded position while engine is already at new load point.",
"Verify repair: actual cam angle tracks desired within 0.2 seconds on scan tool, no hesitation during throttle transients, oil changed at manufacturer recommended interval going forward."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 VVT Oil Control Solenoid and Electrical Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "VVT oil control solenoid degraded \u2014 coil resistance drifted beyond spec, spool valve stuck from varnish, or connector pin corrosion. ECU cannot position phaser: not responding to PWM or responding erratically. Sets P0010/P0020.",
"Scan for DTCs: P0010 or P0020 confirm ECU has detected electrical fault in VVT solenoid circuit. Check freeze-frame data for conditions when fault set (ECT, RPM, oil temperature).",

"Measure solenoid coil resistance at connector with digital multimeter \u2014 compare to manufacturer specification (typically 6-14 ohm at 20 C). Open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance confirms solenoid failure.",
"Check solenoid connector and wiring for green corrosion, broken pins, or chafed insulation. Back-probe ECU-side drive signal with lab scope \u2014 clean PWM waveform confirms ECU driver is good.",

"Remove solenoid and inspect spool valve screen for debris \u2014 clogged screen starves phaser of oil pressure and mimics failed solenoid. Clean screen with solvent. If spool valve does not move freely, replace solenoid.",
"Apply 12 V to solenoid briefly with fused jumper \u2014 spool valve should produce audible click. No click with correct resistance confirms mechanically stuck spool valve.",
"Replace VVT solenoid if confirmed faulty. Use OEM-quality replacement. Verify repair: no P0010/P0020 DTC, actual cam angle tracks desired, connector clean and weather-sealed."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Severe cam/crank misalignment from a jumped timing belt or chain. When the belt jumps one or more teeth (or the tensioner fails completely), valve events occur at the wrong crank angle \u2014 intake valves open during the compression stroke, exhaust valves open during the power str...",

"This is an urgent diagnosis \u2014 if the engine is an interference design, a jumped belt risks piston-to-valve contact and catastrophic engine damage. Do NOT attempt to start or run the engine again until timing is verified.",

"Rotate the engine by hand (socket on the crankshaft bolt) to TDC on cylinder 1 and check cam timing marks. A misalignment of > 2 teeth confirms a jumped belt or chain. Do not force the engine if resistance is felt \u2014 valves may be contacting pistons.",

"If the engine is an interference design and timing has jumped: perform a leak-down test before replacing the timing components. A cylinder with > 50% leakage past the intake or exhaust valves confirms valve-to-piston contact \u2014 the cylinder head must be removed and valves replaced.",
"Verify repair: cam timing marks perfectly aligned at TDC, compression even across all cylinders within 10%, vacuum gauge 17-22 inHg steady at idle, engine runs smoothly throughout the RPM range."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Timing Chain, Belt, and Tensioner Assembly",

"Verify cam timing mechanically at TDC: rotate the engine to TDC on cylinder 1 (compression stroke) and confirm that the camshaft timing marks align exactly with the crankshaft timing mark. Even half a tooth of misalignment confirms timing error.",

"Vacuum gauge at warm idle: a steady but abnormally low reading (10-15 inHg vs 17-22 inHg normal) with the needle steady (not fluctuating) is characteristic of retarded valve timing \u2014 consistent across all cylinders.",

"Check cam/crank correlation with a scan tool: many vehicles report cam/crank phase angle as a PID. Values outside the manufacturer specification (typically +/- 5 degrees) confirm timing error before any mechanical disassembly.",

"Verify repair: cam timing marks aligned at TDC, cam/crank correlation PID within specification, vacuum gauge 17-22 inHg at warm idle, gas analyser shows normal combustion chemistry, engine power restored."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Degraded cerium-oxide washcoat reduces oxygen storage capacity so the post-cat O2 sensor switching ratio approaches 1:1 (mirrors pre-cat), setting P0420/P0430. OSC is depleted through thermal sintering, oil-phosphorus poisoning, or silicon contamination.",
"Rule out feed-gas problems first \u2014 confirm no active P0300\u2013P0312 (misfire), fuel trims within \u00b110 %, no exhaust leak before the rear O2 sensor.",
"Verify the catalyst monitor enable conditions held during the freeze frame: ECT \u2265 70 \u00b0C, steady 2000\u20133000 RPM, closed loop, no misfire DTC.",
"Run Mode $06 catalyst monitor data \u2014 compare the test value to the manufacturer threshold. Within 10 % = borderline; 50 %+ from threshold = genuine failure.",
"Perform IR temperature delta test: outlet weld-ring should be \u2265 20 \u00b0C hotter than inlet at operating temperature. Outlet \u2264 inlet = dead catalyst.",
"After replacement, complete one drive cycle and verify catalyst monitor completes without setting P0420/P0430."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Sustained misfire (> 1 % of combustion events) or persistent rich mixture dumps raw fuel into the catalyst, where exothermic reaction raises substrate temperature above 1000 \u00b0C. The ceramic honeycomb melts, collapses, and creates high exhaust backpressure.",
"Inspect catalyst housing for external discolouration (blue/purple heat staining) \u2014 confirms overheat event.",
"Perform backpressure test at idle and 2500 RPM: idle < 1.5 psi, 2500 RPM < 3.0 psi. Above 3.0 psi at 2500 RPM = confirmed substrate restriction.",
"Remove pre-cat O2 sensor and inspect substrate face with borescope \u2014 look for glassy/glazed or collapsed honeycomb.",
"Replace the catalytic converter. Replace the pre-cat and post-cat O2 sensors if they were exposed to > 1000 \u00b0C.",
"Verify repair: backpressure within spec, tailpipe CO2 \u2265 14.5 %, catalyst monitor completes clean."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Partially collapsed substrate or carbon-clogged honeycomb restricts exhaust flow. Manifold vacuum drops; engine struggles to breathe under load. CO2 collapses at 2500 RPM as volumetric efficiency tanks.",
"Perform backpressure test at idle (should be < 1.5 psi) and 2500 RPM (should be < 3.0 psi). Snap-throttle peak \u2264 5 psi.",
"Inspect substrate face through pre-cat O2 port with borescope \u2014 look for soot plugging or collapsed honeycomb.",
"Verify repair: backpressure at 2500 RPM \u2264 1.5 psi, tailpipe CO2 \u2265 14.5 %, no power loss under load."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Catalyst has lost all conversion capability \u2014 oxidation (CO/HC \u2192 CO2/H2O) and reduction (NOx \u2192 N2) both fail. Tailpipe HC exceeds 250 ppm with-cat, CO above 1.5 %, and NOx breaks through. Post-cat O2 signal is flat at ~0.45 V (atmospheric reference).",
"Confirm dead cat with tailpipe gas analyser: with-cat HC > 250 ppm at 2500 RPM, CO > 1.5 %, CO2 < 13 %. Compare to reference values in master_catalyst_guide.md \u00a77.",
"Verify the problem is the catalyst, not feed-gas: check pre-cat emissions are within normal range (CO ~0.6 %, HC ~100 ppm). If pre-cat is also out of range, the engine is the root cause.",
"IR temperature test: outlet weld-ring temperature \u2264 inlet temperature confirms no conversion is occurring.",
"Check for catalyst poisoning source (oil consumption, coolant leak, RTV silicone) \u2014 identify and repair the poisoning source before replacing the converter.",
"Replace the catalytic converter. Replace post-cat O2 sensor if contaminated.",
"Verify repair: tailpipe HC \u2264 50 ppm, CO \u2264 0.5 %, CO2 \u2265 14.5 % at 2500 RPM. Catalyst monitor completes clean."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "A rich-running engine produces high feed-gas HC and CO, but a healthy catalyst uses stored O2 to oxidise the excess into CO2 and H2O, presenting a clean tailpipe that masks the root engine fault. Strongly negative LTFT confirms the rich feed-gas the catalyst is hiding.",
"Check LTFT \u2014 strongly negative LTFT (< \u221210 %) with clean tailpipe gases is the hallmark of catalyst masking. The cat is scrubbing evidence.",
"Do NOT replace the catalyst. The catalyst is healthy \u2014 it is doing its job. The root cause is upstream (leaking injector, high fuel pressure, EVAP purge stuck open).",
"After repairing the root cause, verify LTFT returns to within \u00b110 % and tailpipe gases remain clean.",
"If the cat has been masking a rich condition for an extended period (> 1000 km), check OSC afterwards \u2014 prolonged rich exposure may have depleted the washcoat."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Engine oil entering the combustion chamber carries phosphorus and zinc from the oil additive package into the exhaust. These elements form a glassy coating on the catalyst washcoat, permanently blocking OSC sites. Gradual P0420 onset over months.",
"Confirm poisoning with borescope inspection of the catalyst face \u2014 look for glassy/glazed coating on the washcoat.",
"Repair the oil consumption root cause before replacing the converter \u2014 a new cat will be poisoned within weeks if the oil path is not closed.",
"Replace post-cat O2 sensor if it shows signs of contamination (white/grey coating on the sensor tip).",
"Verify repair: oil consumption resolved, catalyst monitor completes clean, tailpipe HC \u2264 50 ppm after one drive cycle."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Catalyst fails to reach or maintain light-off temperature (> 250 \u00b0C). Below light-off, CO/HC oxidation and NOx reduction both stall \u2014 the cat passes feed-gas through unconverted. Common causes: failed O2 sensor heater, thermostat stuck open, or short-trip driving pattern.",
"Check pre-cat O2 sensor heater circuit resistance \u2014 failed heater prevents closed-loop entry and delays catalyst warm-up.",
"Verify thermostat opening temperature \u2014 a thermostat stuck open keeps coolant and engine below operating temperature, extending the cold-start enrichment window.",
"Use IR thermometer to measure catalyst inlet weld-ring temperature after 10 minutes of idle \u2014 should exceed 250 \u00b0C. Below 200 \u00b0C = cat never lit off.",
"If the vehicle is used primarily for short trips (< 5 km), the catalyst may never reach light-off \u2014 this is an operating pattern issue, not a fault. Document and advise.",
"If a failed O2 sensor heater or thermostat is found, replace the faulty component.",
"Verify repair: catalyst reaches > 250 \u00b0C within 5 minutes of cold start, closed loop achieved, catalyst monitor completes during drive cycle."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Failed catalytic converter allowing raw fuel to pass through. The catalyst's oxidation capability is destroyed \u2014 hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide pass through unreacted. The gas analyser reads rich (HC 500+ ppm, CO > 1.0%, lambda < 0.98) at the tailpipe while the pre-cat mixtu...",

"Post-cat O2 sensor switching: observe the pre-cat and post-cat O2 sensor waveforms on a scan tool. A healthy catalyst damps the post-cat signal to a nearly flat line. Post-cat switching that mirrors the pre-cat (1:1 switching ratio) confirms the catalyst has no oxygen storage capacity.",
"Check for a P0420/P0430 DTC \u2014 the OBD monitor sets this code when the post-cat O2 switching ratio approaches 1:1, indicating the catalyst OSC has dropped below the fail threshold.",

"Rule out the post-cat O2 sensor as the cause: a lazy or biased post-cat sensor can produce the same switching pattern as a dead catalyst. Swap the post-cat sensor with a known-good sensor or test the sensor response on a gas bench.",

"If the catalyst is confirmed dead and the feed-gas fault is corrected: replace the catalytic converter and both O2 sensors. A catalyst that has seen raw fuel may have a melted or collapsed substrate \u2014 inspect the old catalyst face with a borescope.",
"Verify repair: post-cat O2 flat at ~0.6-0.7 V, tailpipe HC < 50 ppm, CO < 0.5%, lambda at stoichiometric, Mode 06 catalyst monitor passes."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Failed catalytic converter producing a lean tailpipe signature. A dead catalyst that has lost its oxygen storage capacity cannot oxidise CO and HC \u2014 unreacted oxygen from the combustion process passes straight through to the tailpipe. The gas analyser reads elevated O2 with no...",

"Mode 06 catalyst monitor data: review the catalyst monitor test results (typically TID $01-$09, CID $01-$99). A passing catalyst has OSC well above the fail threshold; a marginal or failed catalyst is near or below the threshold.",

"Catalyst temperature test with an infrared thermometer: measure the inlet and outlet temperature of the catalyst at 2500 RPM. A healthy catalyst has an outlet 30-100 C hotter than the inlet (exothermic reaction). Equal or cooler outlet = no reaction = dead catalyst.",

"If the catalyst is confirmed dead: replace the catalytic converter and both O2 sensors (pre- and post-cat). A new catalyst with old sensors inherits any sensor drift that contributed to the original failure.",
"Verify repair: post-cat O2 switching stabilised (flat line near 0.6-0.7 V at steady cruise), Mode 06 catalyst monitor passes, tailpipe emissions within specification."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Fuel trim adaptation has reached its authority limit (typically \u00b125%) in one direction and is holding at the rail \u2014 the ECU can no longer correct the mixture error, confirming a root-cause fault of sufficient magnitude to exceed the trim system's correction range.",

"Record the trim direction: positive saturation (STFT/LTFT pegged at +20 to +25 %) means a lean root cause \u2014 look for vacuum leak, fuel starvation, MAF under-read, injector clog. Negative saturation (pegged at \u221220 to \u221225 %) means a rich root cause \u2014 look for fuel pressure excess, leaking injector, ECT sensor bias, EVAP purge stuck open.",
"ERR-EF-001 is a secondary fault \u2014 it does not replace the root-cause diagnosis; it tells you the correction system is exhausted. Always chase the primary fault first.",

"Check whether trim saturation is bank-specific (STFT1/LTFT1 vs STFT2/LTFT2). Bank-specific saturation points to an injector, coil, or cylinder-specific fault. Global saturation (both banks equal) points to a global air or fuel pressure fault.",
"With the root cause corrected, clear adaptive fuel maps and allow one full warm drive cycle for trim to relearn. Trim should return within \u00b110 % if the fix was complete.",
"If trim does not recover within \u00b110 % after root cause repair, suspect a second independent fault or incomplete repair."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "ECU fuel control is operating in open-loop mode \u2014 the O2 sensor feedback loop is not active \u2014 causing the engine to run at the base calibration map value without trim correction, producing a fixed mixture that is biased by calibration accuracy alone.",

"Confirm open-loop status on scan tool: fuel system status PID should show OL (open loop). If showing CL (closed loop) but trim is frozen at 0 %, suspect a sensor fault (ERR-SF-001, ERR-SF-002) rather than a control system failure.",
"Check for DTC P0140 (O2 sensor no activity \u2014 bank 1) or P0160 (bank 2) \u2014 these specifically flag that the ECU declared the O2 sensor inactive and exited closed-loop.",

"Verify engine coolant temperature: the ECU will remain in open-loop until the ECT sensor reads above the closed-loop entry threshold (typically 70 \u00b0C). Confirm `engine_warmed = true` has been reached (see ERR-SF-005 and ERR-RM-006 for ECT faults that prevent warm-up).",

"Check the upstream O2 sensor heater circuit \u2014 a cold sensor (failed heater) will never produce a switching signal, which is interpreted by many ECUs as sensor absence \u2192 closed-loop disabled.",
"If coolant temp is normal and O2 sensor heater is functional, suspect ECU software fault or calibration corruption. Check for TSBs.",
"After resolving root cause, verify fuel system status transitions to CL within 5 minutes of reaching operating temperature."
"component_group": "Engine Control Module (ECM/PCM) \u2014 Processor and Memory Subsystem",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "ECM internal processor integrity self-check failure \u2014 watchdog timeout, ROM checksum mismatch, KAM corruption, or internal memory fault. ECU self-reports P0606 when its self-test detects a hardware-level fault in the processor or memory subsystem.",

"Verify battery voltage is stable \u2014 check charging system output (13.5\u201314.5 V at 2000 RPM) and battery resting voltage (\u2265 12.4 V). A failing alternator or weak battery can cause intermittent ECU voltage dropout that triggers phantom P0606.",

"Check for companion DTCs \u2014 P0562 (system voltage low), P0563 (system voltage high), P0641 (5V reference open), P0642 (5V reference low), or P0643 (5V reference high) suggest the root cause is power-supply, not the ECU itself.",
"Clear DTCs and re-test under the same operating conditions. If P0606 returns immediately with no companion power-supply DTCs, the ECU internal fault is genuine.",
"Before replacing the ECU, verify the latest ECU calibration/flash is installed \u2014 an incomplete or corrupt flash can set P0606. Re-flash with the latest OEM calibration and re-test.",

"If P0606 persists after re-flash and power-supply faults are ruled out, replace the ECM. Perform immobiliser pairing, CASE relearn (if applicable), and verify all monitors complete one drive cycle without DTC recurrence."

"Check for stored DTCs \u2014 P0606 (ECU internal processor fault), P0601 (memory checksum error), or U-codes (CAN communication faults). Even a single historical occurrence confirms an ECU-side event.",
"Review freeze-frame data for any stored ECU DTCs: note the engine temperature, battery voltage, and vehicle speed at the moment of fault set \u2014 this often reveals the triggering condition.",

"Voltage-drop test on the ECU power and ground circuits under load (headlights, blower, rear defroster on): should be < 0.1 V on the ground side and < 0.3 V on the power side. A marginal ground causes random ECU resets.",

"Heat-soak the ECU with a heat gun (do not exceed 80 C) while monitoring for DTCs or engine-running faults \u2014 a temperature-sensitive internal fault will trigger when the ECU reaches its failure threshold.",
"component_group": "Engine Management \u2014 ECU Injector Driver and MAP Sensor Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "ECU injector-driver leakage or MAP sensor 5V-reference over-voltage causing systematic rich bias. The ECU perceives a leaner mixture than actual, adding fuel until the engine runs truly rich (lambda < 0.98). Gas analyser confirms rich chemistry while ECU data shows positive fu...",

"Scope the injector control signal at a convenient injector connector: look for a clean square-wave with correct pulse width at idle (typically 2-5 ms). A stuck-on signal (constant 12V) or erratic pulse width confirms driver fault.",

"Measure the MAP sensor 5V reference at the MAP sensor connector: should be 5.00 +/- 0.10 V. Above 5.20 V causes the sensor to read higher than actual manifold pressure, which the ECU interprets as higher load, triggering more fuel.",

"Check for coolant contamination at the ECU connector (common on vehicles where the coolant temperature sensor shares a connector with the ECU harness) \u2014 wicking coolant creates a conductive path between pins.",

"If the injector driver is confirmed faulty: the ECU must be replaced or repaired. Verify that the injector itself is not shorted (measure injector resistance, typically 12-16 ohm) \u2014 a shorted injector can damage the new ECU driver.",

"If the MAP sensor reference is over-voltage: check if any other sensor on the same 5V reference circuit is shorted (pull each sensor connector one at a time and re-measure). If all sensors are disconnected and the reference is still high, the ECU voltage regulator is failed.",
"Verify repair: injector waveform clean and correct pulse width, MAP 5V reference within specification, fuel trims within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda."
"component_group": "Engine Management \u2014 ECU Sensor Reference and Ground Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "ECU sensor-ground offset or 5V-reference drift causing systematic lean bias in the fuel control calculation. The ECU perceives a richer mixture than actual (sensor signals shifted higher), pulling fuel trim negative until the engine runs truly lean. Gas analyser confirms lean ...",
"Measure the ECU 5V reference voltage at a convenient sensor (MAF, MAP, or TPS): should be 5.00 +/- 0.10 V. A reading below 4.80 V or above 5.20 V confirms the reference is out of specification.",

"Voltage-drop test on the ECU sensor ground circuit: measure voltage between the sensor ground pin at a sensor connector and battery negative with the engine running. Should be < 0.05 V. Higher values confirm a ground offset.",

"Check for aftermarket accessories tapped into the sensor reference or ground circuits \u2014 piggyback tuning modules, fuel savers, or remote-start systems are common sources of reference-voltage corruption.",

"If the ECU 5V reference or sensor ground is confirmed faulty: inspect the ECU connector for pin corrosion, water ingress, or pin fretting. Clean and re-seat the connector. If the fault persists, the ECU internal voltage regulator or ground plane may be damaged.",
"If the ECU is confirmed faulty: replace or repair the ECU. Do not attempt to compensate with a piggyback signal modifier \u2014 it masks the fault and creates a secondary failure point.",
"Verify repair: ECU 5V reference within specification, sensor ground offset < 0.05 V, fuel trims return to within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Failed manifold-to-head gasket admits air into exhaust stream between cylinder pulses via venturi effect. Upstream O2 reads false-lean, driving positive fuel trim. CO2 stays near normal \u2014 combustion is stoichiometric; only the sample is diluted by the leak.",
"Use an exhaust gas analyser probe near each manifold runner-to-head junction \u2014 HC detection at the joint confirms escaping combustion gas before the O2 sensor.",
"Perform a smoke test via the tailpipe with the engine off \u2014 smoke escaping at the manifold-to-head joint confirms the leak path.",
"Replace the failed exhaust manifold gasket. Inspect the manifold flange for flatness \u2014 a warped flange will cause the new gasket to fail within weeks.",
"Verify repair: O2 sensor switching pattern normalises at 2500 RPM, fuel trims return to within \u00b110 %, cross-counts \u2265 8 in 10 seconds."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Crack in cast-iron or tubular-steel manifold opens under thermal cycling, admitting air pre-O2 sensor. Cast-iron cracks from thermal shock; tubular headers crack at weld stress risers. Leak is pulse-synchronous and louder when cold before expansion closes the gap.",
"Spray a small amount of soapy water near suspected crack points with the engine running cold \u2014 exhaust gas bubbling through the solution confirms the crack location.",
"Remove the exhaust manifold heatshield (if fitted) and visually inspect for carbon trails radiating from the crack \u2014 a black soot line tracing from the fracture confirms the leak.",
"Verify repair: after manifold replacement or weld, O2 sensor switching returns to normal, fuel trims stabilise within \u00b110 %, no exhaust noise."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Bolted flange between manifold outlet and downpipe/cat develops gasket leak. NA engines with O2 in manifold: leak is post-O2 (noise, no trim). Turbo engines with O2 in downpipe: pre-O2 dilution drives false-lean correction and delayed spool from exhaust pressure loss.",
"Cold-engine listening: a sharp metallic ticking at the manifold-to-downpipe flange joint. The noise is loudest at the joint \u2014 use a mechanic's stethoscope or hose to isolate.",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Stainless-steel flex bellows (post-cat) ruptures from engine rocking, corrosion, or impact. Post-cat and post-O2 \u2014 no fuel trim disturbance. Primary symptoms: exhaust noise and cabin fume entry. Check engine mounts: excessive movement causes repeat failure.",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "EGR feed tube (manifold to EGR valve) develops crack or pinhole at weld or flex section. Exhaust escapes before EGR valve, reducing flow. Pre-O2: venturi air ingress drives false-lean O2 readings. Post-O2: noise and reduced EGR flow without fuel trim disturbance.",
"If the leak is pre-O2: check LTFT for positive offset from false-lean correction. Post-O2: no trim effect \u2014 diagnose by noise and visual inspection.",
"Replace the EGR feed tube. Ensure the new tube is correctly torqued at both flare nuts \u2014 over-tightening cracks the flare; under-tightening leaks.",
"After replacement, clear DTCs and verify the EGR monitor completes during a drive cycle without setting P0401 (insufficient flow) or P0402 (excessive flow).",
"Verify repair: no exhaust noise, LTFT within \u00b110 % (if pre-O2), EGR monitor passes."

"If a post-catalyst leak is confirmed: replace the failed gasket, clamp, or pipe section. Post-catalyst leaks do not affect O2 sensor or fuel trim, but they do corrupt the gas sample.",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Pre-O2 exhaust leak admitting atmospheric air into the exhaust stream between cylinder pulses via the venturi effect. Upstream O2 sensor reads false-lean, driving positive fuel trim that over-fuels the engine. The gas analyser sees raw fuel + diluted O2 as a partial-burn (inco...",
"Smoke test via the tailpipe with the engine off: smoke escaping at any pre-O2 joint, gasket, or crack confirms the leak path directly.",

"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 ECU Ignition Driver Transistor / Coil Primary Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "ECU ignition driver transistor degrades thermally, failing to switch coil primary current. Coil fires intermittently or not at all \u2014 misfire stays on cylinder after coil swap, confirming fault is upstream in ECU. Common with high under-hood thermal exposure.",

"Swap the suspect cylinder's ignition coil with a known-good cylinder \u2014 if the misfire stays on the original cylinder (does not follow the coil), the fault is upstream of the coil: wiring, connector, or ECU driver.",

"Back-probe the coil primary control wire with a lab scope \u2014 look for a clean 0\u219212V\u21920 V switching event. A rounded falling edge, missing event, or erratic timing indicates a driver fault.",
"Check the primary circuit wiring between the ECU connector and the coil connector \u2014 resistance should be < 0.5 \u03a9. Any green corrosion at the ECU connector pin suggests water intrusion.",

"If the driver transistor is confirmed failed, the ECU must be replaced or repaired by an ECU specialist. Do not attempt to drive the transistor with an external circuit \u2014 it is part of the ECU's dwell control logic.",
"Verify repair: no misfire DTC, secondary ignition waveform clean across all cylinders, Mode $06 misfire counts at zero."
"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 Ignition Switch and Primary Power Supply Path",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Worn ignition switch contacts create resistive voltage drop in coil primary supply. At cranking or under load, coil voltage drops below 10.5 V, starving coil of dwell current, producing weak or absent spark. Intermittent \u2014 worse hot or with headlights/blower running.",
"Measure voltage at the coil primary supply terminal (usually the coil connector's B+ pin) during cranking \u2014 should be \u2265 10.5 V. Below 10.0 V confirms a supply-side voltage drop.",
"Perform a voltage-drop test across the ignition switch: one probe at battery positive, one probe at the ignition coil supply fuse output, key ON engine running \u2014 drop should be < 0.3 V.",
"Back-probe each side of the ignition switch connector \u2014 if the drop occurs across the switch itself (not the wiring), the switch contacts are worn or corroded.",
"Check that the problem is not caused by aftermarket accessories tapped into the ignition supply circuit (alarm, remote start, stereo) \u2014 these add load and accelerate switch wear.",
"Replace the ignition switch if the voltage drop across the switch exceeds 0.3 V. If the switch is integrated with the immobiliser antenna, a dealer-level key relearn may be required.",
"Verify repair: coil primary voltage \u2265 10.5 V during cranking, no voltage drop across the switch > 0.3 V, misfire counts at zero across all operating conditions."
"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 Crankshaft Position Sensor and Trigger Wheel",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "CKP sensor signal drops out: failing Hall-effect sensor (thermal), cracked VR magnet, excessive air gap, or damaged trigger-wheel tooth. ECU loses crank position reference each dropout, causing random no-spark events registered as P0300 without cylinder-specific DTC.",
"Monitor CKP sensor output with a lab scope while heat-soaking the sensor with a heat gun \u2014 a failing Hall sensor will show dropout or erratic square-wave edges above ~80 \u00b0C.",

"Check the CKP sensor air gap with a feeler gauge against the manufacturer specification (typically 0.5\u20131.5 mm). A loose mounting bolt allows the gap to open beyond the sensor's detection range.",
"Inspect the trigger wheel for a damaged, bent, or missing tooth \u2014 rotate the engine by hand and visually confirm every tooth through the sensor port.",
"If the sensor is a VR (variable reluctance) type, measure coil resistance and check for cracked magnet \u2014 a cracked magnet produces a weak or missing AC signal at low RPM.",
"Verify repair: clean CKP signal at all RPM and temperature conditions, no P0300 or P0335 DTC, misfire counts at zero."
"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 Coil Primary Supply Circuit and Ignition Relay Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Weak spark from compromised coil primary voltage supply \u2014 corroded relay contacts, failing ignition switch, or high-resistance ground. Coil receives insufficient dwell current, producing a weak spark that can ionise the gap but cannot sustain a full flame kernel. Partial combu...",
"Measure coil primary supply voltage at the coil connector B+ pin during engine running \u2014 should be within 0.5 V of battery voltage. A drop > 1.0 V confirms supply-side resistance.",
"Voltage-drop test across the ignition relay: one probe at battery positive, one probe at the coil supply fuse output. Drop should be < 0.3 V. Replace the relay if drop exceeds specification.",
"Inspect the ignition relay socket for signs of overheating (melted plastic, discoloured terminals) \u2014 high resistance at the relay contacts generates heat and accelerates oxidation.",
"Check the coil ground circuit: measure resistance between the coil ground terminal and battery negative \u2014 should be < 0.5 ohm. Clean ground points if high resistance is found.",

"If all supply-side checks pass, test the ignition coil itself with an adjustable spark tester \u2014 spark should jump a 20 mm gap with a bright blue-white arc. Weak orange spark that fails at > 10 mm confirms coil degradation.",
"Verify repair: coil supply voltage within 0.5 V of battery voltage under load, Mode 06 misfire counts at zero, HC within normal range (< 100 ppm) at idle."
"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 Ignition Coil Secondary Winding and Spark Plug Interface",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Ignition coil secondary winding insulation breaks down under heat soak \u2014 spark energy collapses when the coil reaches operating temperature. Cold start is normal; engine stalls or misfires when hot. Swap coil to confirm: misfire follows the coil to the new cylinder.",
"Swap the suspect cylinder's ignition coil with a known-good cylinder \u2014 if the misfire follows the coil, the coil is confirmed faulty.",
"Heat-soak test: run engine to operating temperature, monitor Mode 06 misfire counts. Rising counts on the suspect cylinder as temperature increases confirms thermal breakdown.",
"Measure coil secondary resistance (typically 5-15 kohm at 20 C) \u2014 compare to the manufacturer specification. An open circuit or resistance outside specification confirms failure.",
"Verify repair: no misfire DTC, Mode 06 misfire counts at zero across all cylinders, engine runs smoothly hot and cold."
"component_group": "Ignition System \u2014 Crankshaft Position Sensor and ECU Ignition Control Circuit",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Complete ignition system failure \u2014 no spark on any cylinder despite normal cranking RPM. CKP sensor signal loss, ignition relay failure, or ECU power-supply fault prevents all coil firing. Engine cranks but produces zero combustion \u2014 gas analyser reads ambient air (O2 ~20.9%, ...",
"Read cranking RPM PID during cranking \u2014 0 RPM despite audible cranking confirms CKP sensor failure. Check CKP sensor connector, harness, and sensor air gap.",

"If cranking RPM is normal, disable the fuel pump (pull fuse or relay) and crank while testing for spark with an adjustable spark tester at 20 mm gap. Zero spark on all cylinders confirms global ignition failure.",
"Verify repair: engine starts and runs, no CKP DTC (P0335), Mode 06 misfire counts at zero."

"Heat-soak suspect components with a heat gun while monitoring Mode 06 misfire counts \u2014 a rising count on a specific cylinder as temperature increases confirms a thermal-intermittent coil or sensor.",
"Review freeze-frame data from any stored misfire DTCs \u2014 note the engine temperature, RPM, and load at the moment the fault occurred to identify the triggering condition.",
"Inspect all ignition-related connectors for pin fretting, corrosion, or loose terminal tension \u2014 an intermittent connection can produce a random misfire that is difficult to reproduce.",
"Wiggle-test the ignition wiring harness with the engine running \u2014 listen for RPM drop or misfire counts spiking when a specific connector or harness section is moved.",

"With engine at idle, spray propane or carburetor cleaner carefully around all vacuum hose junctions, intake manifold gasket mating faces, and the throttle body gasket \u2014 RPM change or trim shift confirms the leak location.",
"Use a smoke machine to pressurise the intake downstream of the MAF sensor \u2014 visible smoke escaping identifies the leak point without open-flame risk.",
"Verify repair: fuel trim should recover to within \u00b15 % within 10 minutes of idle."
"Inspect the MAF sensor element visually (requires removal from housing) \u2014 look for oil film, dust coating, or spider webs on the hot-wire or film.",
"Clean the MAF element with dedicated MAF sensor cleaner spray. Do not use brake cleaner or contact cleaner \u2014 they leave residue.",
"Re-test after cleaning: if trims normalise within \u00b15 %, contamination was the cause.",
"If trims do not normalise after cleaning, the element sensitivity is permanently degraded \u2014 replace the MAF sensor.",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Degraded fuel pump delivers insufficient fuel pressure at the rail, causing fuel starvation under demand \u2014 most severe at stress-idle RPM when fuel flow requirements peak.",
"Measure fuel rail static pressure (key-on engine-off) and compare to OEM specification (typically 3.0\u20133.5 bar port injection).",
"Measure fuel pressure at idle and at 2500 RPM \u2014 if pressure drops more than 0.3 bar under load, the pump is confirmed weak.",
"Check the fuel filter first (if accessible and age unknown) \u2014 a clogged filter produces the same low-pressure signature before the pump.",
"Perform a fuel pump current draw test \u2014 a pump drawing more than spec current while producing low pressure indicates impeller wear.",
"Verify repair: pressure holds at OEM spec at 2500 RPM under load."
"Perform a cylinder contribution test at idle \u2014 the affected cylinder shows less HC change when disabled.",
"Attempt ultrasonic injector cleaning on a bench before replacement \u2014 mild deposits can be cleared.",
"If flow rate after cleaning is still > 10 % less than the mean of the set, replace the injector.",
"After replacement, recheck balance test and confirm all cylinders within 5 % of each other."
"Command the EGR valve closed via scan tool (actuator test) and monitor idle quality \u2014 if idle smooths immediately, the valve is confirmed stuck open.",
"Inspect the EGR cooler (if fitted) for internal leaks \u2014 coolant in the exhaust path produces similar dilution.",
"After repair, run a functional EGR test at 2500 RPM \u2014 a healthy EGR valve causes a slight drop in RPM when commanded open at that speed."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "A crack or failed gasket in the exhaust path upstream of the oxygen sensor allows atmospheric air to enter via venturi pulsing, falsely elevating the O2 sensor reading and driving the ECU into unnecessary rich correction.",
"With the engine idling cold, listen for a 'ticking' or 'chuffing' sound from the exhaust manifold area \u2014 exhaust gas escaping through a crack is louder when cold (metal not yet expanded).",
"Use an exhaust gas analyser probe near the suspected leak point \u2014 HC reading at the crack (not the tailpipe) confirms escaping combustion gas.",
"Verify: after repair, O2 sensor switching pattern should normalise and fuel trims return to \u00b15 %."
