"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Ignition and Cam Timing Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Retarded ignition or cam timing producing lean-perceived gas chemistry. Late combustion reduces peak cylinder pressure and temperature, leaving unreacted oxygen in the exhaust that the gas analyser reads as excess air (lambda > 1.02). The engine is not truly lean \u2014 combustion ...",

"Check base ignition timing with a timing light on cylinder 1 \u2014 compare to the manufacturer specification at warm idle. Retarded timing > 5 degrees from specification confirms the timing is late.",

"Verify cam/crank correlation: rotate the engine to TDC on cylinder 1 and confirm that the camshaft timing marks align with the crankshaft timing mark. A misalignment of even one tooth retards all valve events.",

"Vacuum gauge at warm idle: a steady but low reading (10-15 inHg) with minimal needle fluctuation is characteristic of retarded valve timing \u2014 the intake valve closes late, reducing the effective compression stroke.",
"Verify repair: timing marks aligned at TDC, vacuum gauge reads 17-22 inHg at warm idle, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda, engine idles smoothly and power is restored under load."
"component_group": "Ignition System / Fuel System \u2014 Misfire Differential Diagnosis",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Ignition misfire producing a lean-appearing gas signature. A cylinder that does not fire leaves the intake charge (air + fuel) unreacted \u2014 the oxygen passes through to the exhaust analyser, creating a lean reading (elevated O2, lambda > 1.02) that mimics a lean-mixture fault. ...",
"Identify the misfiring cylinder: use Mode 06 misfire counts or a cylinder-balance test (disable one injector at a time and observe the RPM drop \u2014 the dead cylinder shows no RPM change).",
"Swap the ignition coil from the misfiring cylinder to a known-good cylinder \u2014 if the misfire moves, the coil is faulty. If the misfire stays, swap the spark plug next.",

"If coil and plug are ruled out: check the fuel injector for the affected cylinder. A noid light confirms the ECU is commanding injection. Measure injector resistance (typically 12-16 ohm) \u2014 an open circuit confirms a dead injector.",

"Once the root cause of the misfire is identified and repaired, the lean-appearing gas signature will resolve \u2014 the analyser was seeing unreacted oxygen from the dead cylinder, not a true lean mixture.",
"Verify repair: all cylinders contributing equally (cylinder-balance test), Mode 06 misfire counts at zero, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda, HC within normal range (< 100 ppm)."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Cylinder Head Gasket Fire Ring Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Head gasket fire ring breached between two adjacent cylinders. Combustion pressure crosses the gasket land during compression and power strokes \u2014 each cylinder leaks into its neighbour. Compression test shows two adjacent cylinders 30\u201360 psi below the bank average.",

"Compression test all cylinders with throttle wide open \u2014 two adjacent cylinders both reading low (typically 30\u201360 psi below bank average) is the hallmark of a fire-ring breach between them.",
"Leak-down test on each low cylinder: listen at the adjacent spark-plug hole (with that plug removed) \u2014 air escaping confirms the gasket land between them has failed.",
"Block test (chemical) on the cooling system: if positive, the gasket has also breached into a coolant passage \u2014 replace the head gasket immediately to prevent hydrolock.",

"Remove the cylinder head. Inspect the gasket fire ring for a burned-through or crushed section between the two low cylinders. Check the head and block deck for flatness \u2014 resurface if beyond specification.",

"Replace the head gasket with a new MLS or composite gasket per the manufacturer's specification. Torque the head bolts in the correct sequence and to the correct angle specification. Verify repair: compression even across all cylinders, vacuum gauge steady at 17\u201322 inHg."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Cylinder Head Gasket Coolant Passage Seal",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Head gasket breached between a combustion chamber and an adjacent coolant passage. During the power stroke, combustion gas (CO2, HC) is forced into the cooling system at 500+ psi, displacing coolant and over-pressurising the system.",

"Cold engine: remove the radiator cap and start the engine. Watch for a continuous stream of bubbles in the coolant \u2014 this is combustion gas entering the cooling system through the gasket breach.",
"Pressure-test the cooling system to 1.0 bar with the engine off. A rapid pressure drop without an external leak suggests coolant is entering a cylinder through the gasket breach.",
"Check for white exhaust smoke (steam) under load \u2014 coolant entering the combustion chamber vaporises and exits the tailpipe. The exhaust will smell faintly sweet (glycol).",
"Remove the spark plugs after the engine has sat overnight and crank the engine briefly \u2014 coolant droplets ejected from a plug hole confirm that cylinder's gasket has breached to coolant.",

"Replace the head gasket. Flush the cooling system thoroughly to remove any combustion residue. Change the engine oil \u2014 coolant contamination thins the oil and destroys bearing protection. Verify repair: block test negative, no bubbles in coolant, no white smoke under load, cooling system holds pressure."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Piston Ring and Cylinder Bore Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Piston rings worn beyond specification \u2014 compression ring face lost its barrel profile, oil control ring drain-back holes carbon-plugged, or ring tension collapsed from overheat detensioning.",
"Compression test (dry) all cylinders \u2014 affected cylinders read below specification. Record the dry values per cylinder.",

"Wet compression test: add ~1 teaspoon of clean engine oil to each low cylinder through the spark-plug hole and re-test. If compression rises \u2265 20 psi, the rings are worn \u2014 the oil temporarily sealed the ring-to-bore gap. If compression stays low, the leak path is valves or head gasket.",

"Cylinder leak-down test: pressurise each cylinder at TDC compression stroke. Listen at the oil filler cap \u2014 air hissing from the crankcase confirms ring blow-by. Quantify leakage: > 20 % is significant wear.",

"Inspect the PCV system first \u2014 a stuck-closed PCV valve forces crankcase pressure past the rings and mimics ring blow-by. Replace the PCV valve if suspect and re-test before condemning the rings.",

"If rings are confirmed worn: the engine requires a bottom-end rebuild (piston rings, cylinder hone or bore, possibly pistons). This is a major mechanical repair. Verify after rebuild: compression even across all cylinders within 10 %, leak-down < 10 %, no visible blow-by at the oil filler."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Cylinder Head Valve Stem Seal and Guide Assembly",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Valve stem seals hardened, cracked, or worn \u2014 the lip seal no longer wipes oil from the valve stem during guide travel. Oil pools on the back of the valve head when the engine sits, then enters the combustion chamber at startup producing a characteristic blue smoke puff",

"Cold start observation: a distinct puff of blue-white oil smoke from the tailpipe that lasts 2\u20135 seconds then clears completely is the hallmark of valve stem seal leakage. Oil pooled on valve heads during the sit period burns off immediately at startup.",

"Snap-throttle test at operating temperature: hold RPM at ~2500, snap the throttle closed, then snap it open. A plume of blue smoke on the re-open confirms oil was drawn past the intake valve seals during the high-vacuum deceleration phase.",
"Compression test: typically normal across all cylinders. This is the key discriminator vs worn rings \u2014 valve seals leak oil without leaking compression pressure.",

"Leak-down test: air escapes from the intake or exhaust port (not the crankcase), confirming the valve is the leak path. However, this identifies valve seat leakage, not seal leakage \u2014 combined with the smoke pattern, the diagnosis is complete.",

"If only valve stem seals are confirmed: the repair is a cylinder-head-on job \u2014 replace all valve stem seals as a set (intake and exhaust). Inspect valve guides for excessive clearance while the seals are off. Worn guides will destroy new seals within weeks.",

"Verify repair: no blue smoke on cold start, no smoke on snap-throttle, HC at idle within normal range (< 100 ppm). Catalytic converter not poisoned \u2014 if oil consumption was prolonged, check cat efficiency."
"component_group": "Engine Mechanical \u2014 Piston, Ring, and Cylinder Bore Assembly (Global)",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Uniformly low compression across all or most cylinders \u2014 typically 60\u201380 psi across the board from high-mileage ring/cylinder wear, a jumped timing belt/chain, or a severely overheated engine that detensioned all rings simultaneously.",

"Compression test all cylinders dry: if all read uniformly low (e.g. 60\u201380 psi vs 120\u2013180 psi expected), the fault is global \u2014 rings, timing, or a severely overheated engine. Individual low cylinders would point to specific failures.",

"Wet compression test on 2\u20133 representative cylinders: if wet readings rise significantly, rings are the cause of the global low compression. If wet readings do NOT rise, suspect valve timing (jumped belt/chain) or camshaft wear.",

"Check cam timing: rotate the engine to TDC on cylinder 1 and verify that the camshaft timing marks align with the crank timing mark. A jumped timing belt or stretched chain retards cam timing globally, reducing compression across all cylinders.",

"Vacuum gauge at warm idle: a steady but abnormally low reading (10\u201315 inHg instead of 17\u201322 inHg) confirms globally reduced volumetric efficiency from late valve timing or widespread ring wear.",
"Verify repair: compression 120\u2013180 psi across all cylinders within 10 %, vacuum gauge steady 17\u201322 inHg at warm idle, engine idles smoothly, power restored under load."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "One cylinder bore scored \u2014 vertical gouges in the cylinder wall from debris ingestion (broken spark plug electrode, carbon chunk), detonation-eroded piston material smeared on the bore, or oil-starved piston seizure.",

"Compression test all cylinders: one cylinder reads dramatically lower than the rest (30\u201350 psi deficit). Adjacent cylinders are normal \u2014 this is a single-cylinder mechanical fault, not a global issue.",

"Wet compression test on the low cylinder: if compression rises only slightly (< 10 psi increase), oil cannot seal the damage because the bore is physically gouged \u2014 this rules out worn rings and points to bore scoring.",
"Leak-down test on the affected cylinder: listen at the oil filler cap for pronounced crankcase hiss. Quantify: > 30 % leakage confirms severe sealing loss on that cylinder.",

"Remove the spark plug from the affected cylinder and compare to the others \u2014 the affected plug will show heavy oil ash deposits (grey-white crust) while the other plugs are normal. This confirms cylinder-specific oil consumption.",

"Compression test all cylinders dry \u2014 any cylinder below 80% of the manufacturer specification or 100 psi confirms compression loss. Record the dry values per cylinder.",
"Wet compression test on low cylinders: if compression rises > 20 psi, ring wear is confirmed. If compression does NOT rise, the leak is through the valves or head gasket.",

"Inspect the spark plug from the low-compression cylinder \u2014 an oil-fouled plug (wet, black, oily deposit) confirms oil ingress. A steam-cleaned plug (very clean, white) confirms coolant ingress from a head gasket breach.",

"Once mechanical wear is confirmed: the repair depends on the leak path \u2014 rings require a bottom-end rebuild, valves require a cylinder-head rebuild, head gasket requires replacement. This is a major mechanical repair."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Oil consumption from mechanical engine wear producing POA_SIGNATURE chemistry: HC normal to moderately elevated (150-500 ppm), CO low (< 0.5%), lambda near 1.0. Oil enters the combustion chamber past worn rings, valve guides, or seals. Blue-white exhaust smoke is the confirmin...",
"Confirm oil consumption: check the oil level and service history. Consumption > 1 L per 1000 km is significant mechanical wear. Blue-white exhaust smoke confirms oil burning.",
"Cold-start observation: a puff of blue smoke that clears within 2-5 seconds points to valve stem seals. Smoke that persists or worsens under load points to piston rings.",

"Compression test all cylinders dry. Record values. Perform wet compression test on any low cylinders \u2014 a rise > 20 psi confirms ring wear. No rise with low compression points to valve sealing or head gasket.",
"Cylinder leak-down test: pressurise each cylinder at TDC compression. Listen at the oil filler cap \u2014 air hissing confirms ring blow-by. Listen at the intake or exhaust for valve leakage.",

"Inspect the PCV system before condemning the rings \u2014 a stuck-closed PCV valve forces crankcase pressure past the rings and causes oil consumption that resolves when the PCV system is repaired.",
"Swap the suspect COP coil to a known-good cylinder and confirm the misfire DTC follows the coil \u2014 this eliminates injector and compression variables.",
"Inspect the coil boot for white or black tracking marks (carbon arc traces) on the external surface \u2014 visible tracking confirms insulation breakdown.",
"Replace the faulty COP coil. Replace the spark plug on the affected cylinder simultaneously \u2014 arc events often erode the spark plug gap.",
"Remove all spark plugs and inspect \u2014 a carbon-fouled plug shows black matte or oily black deposits across the electrode and insulator nose.",
"Investigate the root cause of fouling: rich running (ERR-RM-001 through ERR-RM-004) causes dry carbon fouling; oil consumption (ERR-RM-001, ERR-RM-002) causes wet oily fouling.",
"Address the root cause \u2014 replacing plugs without fixing the rich or oil-burn condition will cause recurrence within weeks.",
"Remove and measure spark plug gap with a feeler gauge \u2014 a gap more than 0.2 mm above OEM specification confirms erosion.",
"Replace all spark plugs simultaneously \u2014 if one is eroded, the others are typically near end of life.",
"Check ignition coil secondary voltage capacity \u2014 an aged coil may not produce enough peak voltage to fire a correctly-gapped new plug if the coil is also degraded.",
"Verify: misfire DTCs should clear and HC should return to < 100 ppm after one drive cycle."

"Measure primary winding resistance with a multimeter across the coil's primary terminals \u2014 compare to OEM specification (typically 0.5\u20132.0 ohms). An open circuit (\u221e) or short (< 0.3 ohm) confirms failure.",
"Check the ECM coil driver circuit output \u2014 repeated coil primary failures may indicate a failing ECM driver transistor over-driving the coil.",

"Measure injector solenoid resistance with a multimeter \u2014 compare to OEM specification (typically 12\u201316 ohms for high-impedance injectors). An open circuit or < 2 ohms (short) confirms failure.",
"Use a test light or noid light to verify ECM pulse signal reaches the injector \u2014 absence of signal suggests ECM driver failure.",
"Perform a dry compression test on all cylinders \u2014 any cylinder below 80 % of OEM specification or below 689 kPa (100 psi) confirms the problem cylinder.",
"Perform a wet compression test (add oil to the cylinder) \u2014 if compression rises significantly when wet, ring seal is the cause; if no change, valve seating is the cause.",
"Perform a leak-down test to quantify the leak \u2014 listen for air escaping from the intake (valve), exhaust (exhaust valve), or oil cap (rings/bore).",
"This fault requires mechanical repair \u2014 no fuel, ignition, or ECU solution will resolve it."
"Perform a bore scope inspection of the intake ports and valve heads through the intake manifold \u2014 heavy black carbon deposits confirm the diagnosis.",
"Document the cleaning interval \u2014 GDI intake valve carbon typically requires service every 60 000\u2013100 000 km on affected platforms.",

"Review Mode 06 misfire counts per cylinder \u2014 even if no DTC is set (counts are below the P0300 threshold), a cylinder with significantly higher counts than the others identifies the suspect. A healthy cylinder should show near-zero counts.",

"Remove and inspect all spark plugs: measure the gap with a feeler gauge. A gap more than 0.2 mm above OEM specification confirms erosion \u2014 the coil must produce higher voltage to ionise the wider gap, and may fail under load or at high RPM.",

"If spark plugs are within specification: swap the ignition coil from the highest-count cylinder with a known-good cylinder. Ask the patient to drive for one week and return for a Mode 06 re-check \u2014 if the counts moved to the new cylinder, the coil is failing intermittently.",

"For fuel-related intermittent misfire: perform an injector balance test (measure the fuel-pressure drop when each injector is pulsed for a fixed duration). An injector with a significantly different pressure drop confirms a flow problem \u2014 sticky pintle, partial clog, or leaking O-ring.",

"Check for pending DTCs (Mode 07) \u2014 these are DTCs that have failed once but not yet completed the required number of drive cycles for MIL illumination. A pending P0300-P0308 confirms the misfire is real and recurring.",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Rich-mixture misfire from carbon-fouled spark plug that has not yet tripped the OBD misfire monitor. Persistent rich running deposits conductive carbon on the plug insulator, creating a shunt path that bleeds spark energy to ground instead of across the electrode gap. Mode 06 ...",

"Review Mode 06 misfire counts: if counts are elevated but below the P0300 threshold, the misfire is real but the OBD monitor has not yet accumulated enough events to set a DTC. The vehicle may be early in the fault progression.",
"Clear fuel trims and allow the ECU to re-learn after the repair. Monitor Mode 06 misfire counts over one drive cycle \u2014 counts should return to near zero.",

"Verify repair: spark plugs show normal light tan/grey coloration after one tank of fuel, Mode 06 misfire counts at zero, fuel trims within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda, no rich-mixture or misfire DTC."

"Remove all spark plugs and compare \u2014 the plug from the misfiring cylinder will be notably cleaner than the others, with a white, steam-cleaned appearance. This is the single most reliable indicator of coolant entering that cylinder.",

"Pressure-test the cooling system to 1.0 bar with the engine off and the spark plugs removed. A rapid pressure drop + coolant appearing at a spark-plug hole confirms the gasket has breached between the coolant passage and that cylinder.",
"Check for white exhaust smoke (steam) that smells faintly sweet (glycol) \u2014 this confirms coolant is being vaporised in the combustion chamber and exiting the tailpipe.",

"If the head gasket coolant breach is confirmed: the cylinder head must be removed and the gasket replaced. Inspect the head and block deck for flatness \u2014 an overheated engine often warps the head, requiring resurfacing.",

"Verify repair: block test negative, cooling system holds pressure, no white smoke, spark plugs show normal coloration across all cylinders, Mode 06 misfire counts at zero, compression even across all cylinders."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Weak spark (coil degradation, fouled plugs, low cranking voltage) or poor fuel atomisation \u2014 marginal combustion never sustains. Gas: HC moderate (300 ppm), CO low (0.02 %), CO2 depressed (4 %), O2 high (16 %), lambda lean (1.35). Intermittent firing not enough to reach idle.",
"Check battery voltage during cranking \u2014 below 10.0 V starves the ignition coils and injectors of operating voltage. Charge or replace battery before further diagnosis.",

"Remove and inspect all spark plugs \u2014 look for wet fouling (fuel present, no spark), carbon fouling (weak spark can't ionise gap), or gap erosion beyond spec. Replace plugs if any are marginal.",
"Test ignition coil secondary with an adjustable spark tester \u2014 spark should jump a 20 mm gap with a bright blue-white arc. Weak orange spark that fails at >10 mm = marginal coil.",
"Verify fuel pressure under load during cranking \u2014 marginal pump may produce KOEO pressure but collapse during extended cranking. Pressure should hold within 10 % of spec throughout cranking.",

"If all of the above checks pass, perform a relative compression test: read cranking RPM and MAP during cranking. Uneven cranking speed or MAP pulses indicate compression loss \u2014 route to compression test.",
"Verify repair: engine starts consistently. Gas analyser shows normal cold-start enrichment transitioning to stoichiometric idle within 60 seconds."
"Check cranking RPM via PID. 0 RPM confirms CKP sensor failure.",
"Verify spark with adjustable spark tester. Must jump 20 mm gap.",

Gas analyser reads lean: lambda > 1.20, HC low (< 100 ppm), ...",
"KOEO (Key On, Engine Off) fuel pressure test: pressure must reach the manufacturer specification within 2 seconds of key-on. Zero pressure confirms fuel pump or relay failure.",
"Noid light test at a fuel injector connector during cranking \u2014 a flashing noid light confirms the ECU is commanding fuel delivery. No flash confirms an injector-circuit or CKP-signal fault.",
"Check the fuel-pump relay: swap with an identical relay from a non-critical circuit. Listen for the fuel pump prime (2-second hum at key-on) \u2014 silence confirms pump or relay failure.",

"If the pump does not run: check for battery voltage at the pump connector during the 2-second prime window. Voltage present but pump silent = failed pump motor. No voltage = open circuit between the relay and pump (wiring, inertia switch, or connector).",

"Verify repair: engine starts within 2 seconds of cranking, fuel pressure holds within 10% of specification at idle and under load, gas analyser shows stoichiometric mixture within 60 seconds of cold start."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Ignition coil primary or secondary failure preventing spark generation on all cylinders. Engine cranks with normal RPM (150-300 via PID 0C) but produces zero combustion. "Confirm cranking RPM is normal via PID 0C to rule out CKP sensor failure. 0 RPM routes to CKP diagnosis.",
"Disable the fuel pump by pulling the fuel-pump fuse or relay. Crank the engine and test for spark at each cylinder with an adjustable spark tester at 20 mm gap.",

Each firing event is too weak to accelerate the crankshaft enough for the next cylinder to fire. Gas shows moderate HC (200-800 ppm), depressed CO2 (3-6%), high O2 (12-18%)...",
"Check battery voltage during cranking \u2014 below 10.0 V starves both ignition coils and injectors of operating voltage. Charge or replace the battery before further diagnosis.",
"Remove and inspect all spark plugs \u2014 look for wet fouling (fuel present but no spark), carbon fouling (weak spark cannot ionise the gap), or gap erosion beyond specification.",

"Test ignition coil secondary with an adjustable spark tester \u2014 spark should jump a 20 mm gap with a bright blue-white arc. Weak orange spark that fails at > 10 mm confirms marginal coil output.",

"Verify fuel pressure holds during extended cranking \u2014 a marginal fuel pump may produce KOEO pressure but collapse under load. Pressure should stay within 10% of specification throughout cranking.",

"If all of the above pass, perform a relative compression test: monitor cranking RPM and MAP during cranking. Uneven cranking speed or MAP pulses indicate compression loss \u2014 route to a full compression test.",

"Check the fuel-pump relay contacts for pitting or oxidation \u2014 an intermittent relay can prime at key-on but drop out during cranking. Swap with a known-good relay and ask the patient to monitor.",
"Monitor the CKP sensor signal with a lab scope while heat-soaking the sensor \u2014 a failing sensor may show dropout or erratic edges above ~80 C that recover when cool.",

"Check the ignition switch for voltage drop: measure the voltage at the ignition coil supply fuse during cranking. A momentary drop below 10.0 V followed by recovery confirms switch contact degradation.",
"Inspect the valve cover gasket area and breather hoses for oil weeping \u2014 confirms oil is migrating.",
"Verify repair: retest HC at idle and confirm drop below 120 ppm."
"Check crankcase ventilation \u2014 excessive blow-by pressure (pop-up dipstick, white smoke from breather) confirms ring leakage.",
"If compression < 80 % of OEM spec or leak-down > 20 %, engine requires overhaul (rings/bore resizing).",
"Remove injectors and bench-test flow and leak-back \u2014 a leaking seat drips more than 1 drop per 30 seconds at rail pressure.",
"Check fuel rail pressure hold-down after pump off \u2014 rapid pressure loss confirms internal injector leak.",
"Recheck with scan tool: short-term fuel trim should return to within \u00b15 % after replacement.",
"If all injectors are leaking, suspect contaminated fuel or injector age \u2014 consider full set replacement."
"Disconnect the EVAP purge hose from the intake manifold port; if the engine smooths and trims recover toward 0 %, the purge valve is confirmed stuck open.",
"Apply vacuum to the purge valve solenoid with the ignition off \u2014 a healthy valve should hold vacuum indefinitely; a stuck valve bleeds down.",
"Check the carbon canister for saturation (fuel-soaked canister vents fuel not vapour \u2014 replace canister if saturated).",
"After repair, verify EVAP system integrity with a smoke test and confirm trim recovery within \u00b15 %."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Rich-mixture root cause with lean overshoot at idle from aggressive ECU fuel-trim correction. An underlying rich condition (elevated fuel pressure, leaking injector, or EVAP vapour intrusion) drives LTFT strongly negative. At idle \u2014 the lowest fuel-demand operating point \u2014 the...",

"Check fuel pressure at the rail at idle and under load: elevated pressure (above specification) confirms a fuel-pressure regulator fault or restricted return line. A vacuum-referenced regulator should drop pressure by ~0.3 bar when vacuum is applied.",

"Perform an injector leak-down test: pressurise the fuel rail (KOEO), then observe pressure decay over 10 minutes. A rapid pressure drop with no external leak confirms an injector is dripping into the intake.",

"Check LTFT: strongly negative LTFT (< -15%) with the gas analyser reading lean at idle is the signature of this pattern \u2014 the ECU is over-correcting a rich condition, overshooting into lean at low fuel demand.",
"Verify repair: fuel pressure within specification, LTFT returns to within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda at both idle and under load, EVAP monitor passes without DTC."
"component_group": "Ignition System / Fuel System \u2014 Misfire Differential Diagnosis",

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Ignition misfire producing a rich-perceived gas signature. A dead cylinder passes the full intake charge (air + unburned fuel) directly into the exhaust, where the gas analyser reads raw hydrocarbons (HC 1000+ ppm) and depressed oxygen \u2014 the classic rich-mixture pattern on a n...",

"Identify the dead cylinder: use Mode 06 misfire counts, a cylinder-balance test, or an infrared thermometer on the exhaust manifold runners (the dead cylinder's runner will be significantly cooler).",

"Confirm spark on the dead cylinder: remove the spark plug, reconnect it to the coil, ground the plug body, and crank. A bright blue-white spark confirms the ignition system is functioning \u2014 the fault is fuel or mechanical.",

"If both spark and fuel are confirmed: perform a compression test. A cylinder that has spark and fuel but does not fire has a mechanical fault \u2014 zero compression from a holed piston, stuck valve, or severe head-gasket breach.",
"Once the root cause of the misfire is corrected, the rich-appearing gas signature resolves \u2014 the analyser was seeing unburned fuel from the dead cylinder, not a true rich mixture.",
"Verify repair: all cylinders firing, Mode 06 misfire counts at zero, HC below 100 ppm at idle, lambda at stoichiometric, no fuel smell in the exhaust."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Degraded upstream O2 sensor element responds slowly to exhaust mixture changes, causing the ECU's closed-loop fuel control to oscillate sluggishly and over-correct, producing erratic trim behaviour without a true rich or lean condition.",

"Observe the upstream O2 sensor switching frequency on a scan tool in live data \u2014 a healthy narrowband sensor should switch > 0.5 Hz (ideally 1\u20132 Hz) at warm idle; a lazy sensor switches < 0.25 Hz or holds mid-voltage.",
"Check O2 sensor heating circuit \u2014 if the heater has failed, the sensor runs colder and responds slower; measure heater circuit resistance.",
"Note: the gas analyser lambda_chem value is the ground truth. If lambda_chem is near 1.0 but the O2 sensor signal is not switching normally, the sensor is suspect.",
"After replacement, verify switching frequency returns to > 0.5 Hz and fuel trim settles within \u00b15 % at warm idle.",
"Verify the downstream O2 sensor shows normal differential from upstream (confirms catalyst is also healthy)."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Dead upstream O2 sensor element locks at a fixed output voltage, forcing the ECU into an erroneous fixed-mixture belief and either opening the loop or driving extreme trim adaptation in one direction continuously.",
"Observe the upstream O2 sensor voltage in scan tool live data \u2014 a stuck-rich sensor reads > 0.7 V indefinitely; a stuck-lean sensor reads < 0.2 V indefinitely. No switching occurs.",

"Check O2 sensor heater circuit \u2014 a failed heater that never brings the sensor to operating temperature (> 300 \u00b0C) causes a stuck near-zero voltage from a cold element (cold O2 sensor = lean voltage).",
"After replacement, verify the sensor begins switching within 30 seconds of engine start (heater brings it to temp quickly on a new sensor).",
"Compare the MAF reading (g/s) on the scan tool to the expected value for the engine's idle RPM and displacement \u2014 typical idle MAF is 2\u20138 g/s per litre of displacement.",
"Check MAF signal plausibility: if the MAF reads low at idle AND the engine is running lean (trim > +15 %), suspect MAF hardware failure.",
"Try cleaning the MAF element with dedicated MAF cleaner first \u2014 if contamination is the cause, trim will recover (see ERR-LC-002).",
"After replacement, verify g/s reading matches expected for the engine size and trim returns to \u00b15 %.",
"Check that the new MAF sensor matches the OEM part number \u2014 aftermarket MAF sensors are a known source of persistent lean codes."
"With ignition on, engine off: MAP sensor should read close to barometric pressure (typically 100\u2013103 kPa at sea level). Any reading more than 3 kPa off is suspect.",
"With engine at warm idle: MAP should read 30\u201350 kPa (naturally aspirated idle vacuum). A reading significantly higher or lower at known-good idle conditions confirms drift.",
"Compare MAP reading to expected vacuum on the fuel trim graph \u2014 if the MAP is high (under-reading vacuum) when trims are positive, a lean bias from the MAP is confirmed.",
"Compare ECT sensor reading on scan tool to actual coolant temperature measured with a contact thermometer at the thermostat housing \u2014 a > 15 \u00b0C discrepancy confirms sensor failure.",

"Inspect the thermostat: a thermostat stuck open produces genuinely cold coolant (the sensor reads correctly but the engine never warms up) \u2014 feel the upper radiator hose. Hot hose at idle = thermostat open (mechanical fault). Cold hose = sensor fault (sensor wrong, engine actually warming normally).",
"After replacement, verify ECT on scan tool matches contact thermometer within 5 \u00b0C at operating temperature.",
"Confirm ECU enters closed-loop (fuel system status = CL) within 5 minutes of reaching normal operating temperature."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Contaminated downstream O2 sensor produces a signal pattern that mimics a failed catalyst \u2014 switching where it should be flat \u2014 triggering false P0420/P0430 catalyst efficiency DTCs when the catalyst is mechanically intact.",

"Verify catalyst efficiency test conditions: coolant temp > 80 \u00b0C, no misfire DTCs, no fuel trim beyond \u00b110 %. If any precondition is broken, fix it first and retest \u2014 false P0420 is common when fuel trim is skewed.",

"Compare upstream vs downstream O2 sensor waveforms in live data. A healthy catalyst: downstream is nearly flat (< 0.5 Hz switching). A contaminated downstream sensor: switching at nearly the same frequency as the upstream sensor.",
"Inspect downstream O2 sensor connector and bung for moisture, oil residue, or coolant seepage \u2014 these are the common contamination routes.",
"Substitute a known-good downstream sensor (or a new one) and retest \u2014 if P0420 does not return over one complete drive cycle, the original sensor was the fault.",
"If P0420 returns after sensor replacement, the catalyst itself is confirmed defective (ERR-EF-003 boundary \u2014 out of scope v1).",
"component_group": "Engine Management \u2014 Air Metering and Temperature Sensors",

"Compare MAF reading at warm idle against the manufacturer specification (typically 2-6 g/s for a 2.0 L engine). A reading consistently below specification with normal idle quality suggests sensor under-read.",
"Clean the MAF sensor hot-wire with a dedicated MAF cleaner spray \u2014 do NOT use brake cleaner, carb cleaner, or any solvent that leaves a residue. Allow to dry completely before re-installing.",

"Check the MAP sensor vacuum hose for cracks, kinks, or oil contamination \u2014 a restricted vacuum signal causes the MAP sensor to under-report manifold pressure, which the ECU interprets as lower load.",

"Compare IAT reading at cold start against the ambient temperature and ECT reading \u2014 all three should agree within a few degrees. An IAT reading that is consistently higher than the other two confirms sensor drift.",
"Verify repair: MAF/MAP/IAT readings within specification, fuel trims within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda, no lean-mixture DTC returns."

"mechanical_failure_mode": "Temperature or pressure sensor over-reading, causing the ECU to over-fuel and create true rich combustion. ECT sensor biased cold (stuck at low resistance, reading -40 C on a warm engine), fuel-rail pressure sensor reading high, or MAF over-reading from oil-saturated hot-wire ...",

"Compare ECT reading on a scan tool against the mechanical thermostat housing temperature (infrared thermometer) on a fully warmed engine \u2014 should agree within 5 C. An ECT reading significantly colder confirms sensor drift.",

"Measure ECT sensor resistance and compare to the manufacturer's temperature/resistance table \u2014 a sensor that reads 2-3 kohm at 90 C should read > 10 kohm at 20 C. A stuck-low resistance (cold reading) forces cold-start enrichment continuously.",

"Check the fuel-rail pressure sensor reading against a mechanical fuel-pressure gauge \u2014 if the sensor reads higher than actual, the ECU reduces injector pulse width thinking pressure is higher, but the error is typically in the opposite direction. A sensor reading low drives the ECU to increase pulse width, creating rich.",

"Inspect the MAF sensor for oil contamination from an over-oiled aftermarket air filter \u2014 the oil film on the hot-wire insulates it, causing the sensor to over-read air mass, which the ECU compensates with more fuel.",
"Verify repair: sensor readings within specification against known-good references, fuel trims return to within +/-10%, gas analyser shows stoichiometric lambda, no rich-mixture DTC returns."

"description": "Mechanical base timing error (non-VVT): physical camshaft timing is incorrect due to belt/chain misalignment, independent of VVT system. Produces CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF chemistry \u2014 elevated HC + CO with depressed CO2. No cam sensor DTC expected on non-VVT engines. v1 ERR-CT-001 reactivated, map_kpa constraint removed (no MAP data in curated corpus for any cam_timing case). This is the only cam_timing rule without a VVT precondition \u2014 closes the v1 gap where 4 of 5 rules required vvt_equipped",

"description": "VVT phaser malfunction \u2014 retard / lag pattern: VVT phaser is sluggish, stuck retarded, or lagging under load. Produces VVT_FAILURE chemistry \u2014 elevated HC, depressed CO2, low NOx (<80 ppm). The low NOx differentiates cam_timing from lean_condition (NOx >800 ppm). Typically accompanied by P0011 (cam over-advanced) or P0012 (cam over-retarded). TIMING_RETARDED chemistry accepted as SUGGESTIVE evidence \u2014 closes the ~3-case Tier B gap for cam_timing. OBD evidence: fuel trims mildly elevated (stft > 2.0) as SUGGESTIVE \u2014 phaser lag causes the ECU to compensate with positive trims. v1 ERR-CT-003 reactivated with TIMING_RETARDED evidence added",

"description": "IGNITION_MISFIRE chemistry with cam timing: VVT phaser malfunction produces late combustion \u2192 incomplete burn \u2192 IGNITION_MISFIRE chemistry. The cam timing fault mimics misfire emissions (high HC, elevated CO, normal O2) but the root cause is valve timing, not ignition. Differentiated from misfire family by VVT DTC presence (P0011/P0012) as DEFINITIVE \u2014 the DTC is the key discriminator when chemistry is shared (FT-10). v1 ERR-CT-002 reactivated",

"description": "VVT phaser stuck advanced with negative fuel trims: VVT phaser is over-advanced, causing knock and rich combustion. Produces VVT_FAILURE chemistry. Differentiated from CT-002 (retard pattern) by negative fuel trim evidence \u2014 the advance/knock pattern pushes trims negative as ECU pulls fuel. OBD: stft_b1 < -5.0 and ltft_b1 < -5.0 as SUGGESTIVE. Accompanied by P0011 or P0012. v1 ERR-CT-004 expanded with DTC and OBD evidence to replace the v1 GAS_ONLY at 0.55 confidence",

"description": "VVT solenoid/actuator electrical fault: VVT solenoid coil resistance drift or actuator circuit fault. Gated on VVT_HISTORY range DTCs (P0010-P0023) \u2014 at least one VVT DTC must be present. No chemistry requirement \u2014 the electrical nature of the fault means chemistry may be NORMAL_OPERATION or ambiguous. OBD: fuel trims near zero (stft_b1 in_range [-5,5], ltft_b1 in_range [-5,5]) as SUGGESTIVE \u2014 solenoid drift causes marginal trim response, not the saturation pattern seen in ecu_fault. Confidence ceiling applied \u2014 sole DTC-primary rule in the cam_timing set. EXP-N023 (no DTC, no MAP, no RPM) is NOT covered and is documented as an Unplanned follow-up",

"description": "TIMING_RETARDED chemistry with cam timing DTCs \u2014 Tier B gap closer: GASLab emits TIMING_RETARDED chemistry (elevated HC, depressed CO2, combustion phasing delayed) as a secondary effect of VVT phaser malfunction. Gated on VVT_HISTORY DTCs (P0011-P0024) \u2014 at least one VVT DTC must be present for this rule to evaluate. TIMING_RETARDED chemistry is SUGGESTIVE evidence, not a GATING condition \u2014 this rule competes with CT-002 on TIMING_RETARDED cases where VVT DTCs are also present. Confidence ceiling applied because TIMING_RETARDED chemistry is shared across 7 families and cam_timing is not the only consumer",

"description": "VVT-DTC bridge for shared bad-combustion chemistry: GASLab can emit INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION, SAMPLE_INVALID, or VVT_FAILURE on cam timing cases that carry P0011/P0012. The VVT DTC is GATING so this rule cannot fire on generic misfire-like chemistry without cam timing evidence. FT-10",

"description": "No-DTC non-VVT cam timing bridge: mechanical base timing error can surface as INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION instead of CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF. This rule is tightly bounded to the observed non-VVT gas window and gates out lean, misfire, and VVT DTC paths so it does not become a generic incomplete-combustion catch-all. FT-10",
"description": "Cam phasing retarded on a MAP-sensed (speed-density) engine: GASLab CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP chemistry. The MAP-system twin of CT-001.",
"description": "Cam phasing advanced: GASLab CAM_TIMING_ADVANCED chemistry (HC 250-600 ppm at idle, NOx rising and HC falling idle to 2500).",
"description": "Dead or overwhelmed catalyst \u2014 post-cat gases show failed reduction: high NOx breakthrough, depressed CO2, with P0420/P0430 DTC confirmation",

"description": "Catalyst masking \u2014 cat cleans tailpipe to pristine levels (NORMAL_OPERATION chemistry) but elevated LTFT reveals upstream mechanical wear or oil burn the cat is compensating for; perception_flag: tailpipe is perception, OBD trims are the tell",
"description": "Flow restriction \u2014 melted or collapsed catalyst substrate causes exhaust backpressure: CO2 collapses under load, O2 rises as exhaust backs up, often with P0420 set",
"description": "Cold catalyst / not lighting off \u2014 cat below light-off temperature from heater circuit failure or low ECT; downstream O2 fluctuates, P0420 set despite engine being healthy",

"description": "TIMING_RETARDED-aware marginal catalyst \u2014 knock-avoidance timing pull masks catalyst degradation; accepts TIMING_RETARDED as suggestive evidence rather than gating hard on CATALYST_OVERWHELMED, closing the Tier B chemistry gap for ~10 catalyst_failure cases",

"description": "Perception-gap catalyst failure \u2014 Brettschneider override: chemistry shows CATALYST_OVERWHELMED but OBD lambda is zero or significantly biased (ECU O2 sensor perception failure); chemistry lambda is ground truth, OBD lambda is perception",

"description": "Marginal HC breakthrough \u2014 early-stage catalyst degradation where HC rises under load but cat hasn't fully collapsed; includes freeze-frame-only evidence where idle gases are pristine but drive-cycle freeze frame shows cat failure",

"description": "System voltage fault (low or high) \u2014 P0562 (system voltage low) or P0563 (system voltage high) is the pathognomonic charging-system DTC. DTC-only diagnosis; the schema does not capture battery voltage telemetry.",

"description": "Charging-induced ghost misfire \u2014 ECU reports P0300 random misfire on a vehicle with a charging-system DTC and clean combustion chemistry. The misfire is electrical-sensor noise from voltage instability, not a real combustion failure. NORMAL_OPERATION chemistry at tier GATING is the discriminator from misfire-family rule MF-004 (which gates on NORMAL chemistry DEFINITIVE without requiring a charging DTC).",

"description": "Fuel trim saturated \u2014 positive (max enrichment): ECU has adapted fuel trims to maximum positive limit, adding fuel against a perceived lean condition that contradicts the gas analyser. Long-term and short-term trims both pegged high. Typically accompanied by P0171 (System Too Lean) but the gas analyser shows rich or stoichiometric \u2014 the ECU is being deceived. Truth-vs-perception: ECU perceives lean, gas analyser shows rich or normal. v1 orphan ERR-EF-001 (fuel_trim_saturated) reactivated, positive polarity",
"precondition": "longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame",

"description": "Fuel trim saturated \u2014 negative (max enleanment): ECU has adapted fuel trims to maximum negative limit, pulling fuel against a perceived rich condition that contradicts the gas analyser. Long-term and short-term trims both pegged low. Typically accompanied by P0172 (System Too Rich) but the gas analyser shows lean or stoichiometric \u2014 the ECU is being deceived by a biased sensor. Truth-vs-perception: ECU perceives rich, gas analyser shows lean or normal. v1 orphan ERR-EF-001 (fuel_trim_saturated) reactivated, negative polarity",
"precondition": "longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame",

"description": "Closed-loop fuel control disabled / trims frozen: ECU has disabled closed-loop fuel control \u2014 both long-term and short-term fuel trims are frozen at or near zero because the ECU cannot trust its sensor inputs. Accompanied by DTCs indicating ECU-level faults (P0606 ECU internal), sensor circuit faults that force open-loop (P0113 IAT circuit high, P0118 ECT circuit high), injector driver faults (P0201-P0206), or coolant thermostat faults (P0128). The ECU has given up adapting \u2014 the trims tell the story. v1 orphan ERR-EF-002 (closed_loop_fuel_control_disabled) reactivated",
"precondition": "longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame",

"description": "ECU internal fault \u2014 DTC-driven: ECU has logged an internal hardware or software fault (P0600-P0699 range, ECU_INTERNAL_HISTORY). These are processor, memory, or calibration integrity faults detected by the ECU's own self-diagnostics. TIMING_RETARDED chemistry may appear as a secondary symptom when the ECU limits ignition timing in response to the internal fault (~10 ecu_fault cases produce this chemistry in the curated corpus). No OBD gate \u2014 the ECU internal DTC alone gates this rule. This is the only ecu_fault rule that carries a chemistry evidence slot (TIMING_RETARDED SUGGESTIVE), closing the Tier B gap for ecu_fault",

"description": "SAMPLE_INVALID with ECU fault: GASLab's triangle-gate rejects the sample as unphysical (CO+CO2+O2 outside [14,16]), typically because the ECU fault has corrupted sensor data or caused a measurement anomaly. SAMPLE_INVALID chemistry gates this rule \u2014 it only evaluates when GASLab emits SAMPLE_INVALID. When the triangle fails AND ECU-fault-indicative DTCs are present (P0171/P0172 fuel trim codes or P0606 ECU internal), the unphysical gas reading is attributed to ECU control failure rather than an analyser problem. Covers the ~2 SAMPLE_INVALID ecu_fault cases identified in the chemistry coverage matrix",

"description": "Pre-cat exhaust leak \u2014 false air enters before upstream O2 sensor at manifold flange or header gasket: O2 sensor reads lean, ECU compensates with positive LTFT, chemistry confirms air dilution via elevated O2. Collapses v1's four LTFT-threshold variants (ERR-EL-001/002/003/005) into one evidence-accumulation rule",

"description": "Post-cat exhaust leak \u2014 leak between upstream and downstream O2 sensors: downstream O2 sees excess oxygen (lean), confounds catalyst efficiency diagnosis, P2096/P2098 'Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean' DTC sets. Chemistry confirms air dilution; downstream O2 lean signal is the anatomical differentiator from pre-cat leaks",

"description": "Probe-tip or manifold leak \u2014 false air enters at sample probe, header flange, or exhaust joint: HC and O2 both read elevated from dilution (ambient air mixes with exhaust sample). No DTC required \u2014 the gas chemistry is the primary signal. Differentiated from EL-001 by HC elevation and absence of mandatory LTFT or DTC evidence",

"description": "ECU ignition coil driver fault — IGNITION_MISFIRE chemistry with coil-primary DTC (P0351–P0358) and positive short-term fuel trim confirms the misfire is ignition-hardware, not fuel or mechanical. Reproduces e2e ERR-IF-001 path.",

"description": "Knock-sensor-indicated pre-ignition / weak spark — POA_SIGNATURE chemistry with knock-sensor DTC (P0324–P0334) and elevated HC. Knock-sensor circuit faults are an ignition-system discriminator: pre-ignition and knock events stress the secondary ignition, and a knock DTC without a misfire DTC points to ignition hardware rather than fuel/mechanical. GATING on knock DTC prevents cannibalisation of other POA_SIGNATURE families. base_weight 0.86: on POA_SIGNATURE cases scores 1.01→1.0 (0.86 + 0.10 DEF + 0.05 SUGG); on SAMPLE_INVALID/chemistry-None cases (where the shim blanks chemistry per hard-absence semantics) scores 0.91 (0.86 + 0.05 SUGG), clearing CF-001 at 0.90 on both consumer cases.",

"description": "Late ignition timing / no-DTC ignition fault — POA_SIGNATURE chemistry (catch-all, variable gas signature) with elevated HC and no DTC requirement. Captures ignition-timing faults (knock-sensor fault causing late spark, failing coil producing weak spark below the misfire-detection threshold) that the ECU does not flag with a DTC. Low base_weight (0.42) prevents cannibalisation of other POA_SIGNATURE families: this rule fires at 0.57 (0.42 + 0.10 + 0.05) which beats no_fault but loses to any other family with a stronger signal. Known limitation: cannot flip case_036 (current winner CF-001 at 0.90) without raising base_weight above 0.75, which would cannibalise all POA_SIGNATURE cases — see progress_notes.",
"description": "CO2 over physical maximum \u2014 exceeds the ~16% theoretical ceiling for gasoline stoichiometric combustion; physically impossible, therefore input data is invalid",
"description": "Near-atmospheric oxygen with depleted CO2 \u2014 open-air or false-air signature indicating sample contamination, not combustion exhaust",
"description": "Classic lean condition from unmetered air \u2014 Brettschneider lambda > 1.03 with positive fuel trims",

"description": "Lean condition with retarded timing \u2014 knock-avoidance timing pull causes lean chemistry without DTC confirmation. LEAN_MIXTURE is GATING (T-COMA-28, F-C1-2): without lean chemistry the rule does not fire on normal idle vacuum alone",
"description": "MAF sensor contamination or under-reading \u2014 low airflow signal causes ECU to under-fuel producing lean exhaust",

"description": "Worn piston rings / oil consumption: oil slips past rings into combustion chamber, elevating HC. At higher RPM ring flutter improves sealing and HC drops \u2014 the opposite pattern of lean_condition where HC rises with RPM. Chemistry-primary rule: WORN_PISTON_RINGS as GATING evidence. v1 ERR-MW-003 reactivated with the shrtft1 IN_RANGE [-10,10] constraint removed \u2014 oil burning can foul O2 sensors, making trim-based constraints unreliable for ring-wear detection. OBD: hc > 200 ppm DEFINITIVE \u2014 ring-wear HC elevation exceeds the misfire hc>200 SUGGESTIVE, giving MW a structural advantage on high-HC cases (FT-10)",

"description": "Worn valve stem seals: oil leaks past valve stem seals into combustion chamber under high vacuum (snap-throttle closed / deceleration). Produces WORN_VALVE_SEALS chemistry \u2014 transient HC plume, not steady-state elevation. Differentiated from ring wear (MW-001) by the transient/snap-throttle HC pattern vs steady elevated HC. v1 ERR-MW-004 reactivated (v1 was GAS_ONLY at 0.70). confidence_ceiling applied because this is the only WORN_VALVE_SEALS-gated rule in the competition group",

"description": "Coolant in combustion / head gasket breach: coolant enters combustion chamber through failed head gasket, quenching combustion. Produces COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL chemistry \u2014 elevated HC + elevated O2 + depressed CO2 simultaneously. OBD: ect_c > 95.0 degC as SUGGESTIVE (coolant loss concentrates heat in remaining coolant, raising sensor reading). v1 ERR-MW-002 expanded (v1 had ect_c > 90.0 only; v2 tightens to 95.0 and adds chemistry-primary architecture)",

"description": "Low compression / worn engine (general wear): cylinder sealing failure from worn rings, scored bores, or burned valves produces WORN_ENGINE chemistry \u2014 severely depressed CO2 (<12%) from incomplete combustion. No OBD evidence: the former map_kpa < 30.0 kPa row tested strong vacuum, the opposite of weak cylinders (T-COMA-32); a weak-vacuum MAP floor needs a verified value. v1 ERR-MW-006 expanded with MAP evidence (v1 had no OBD constraints). INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION is DEFINITIVE \u2014 mechanical_wear is the primary consumer of this chemistry; misfire has no INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION rule (FT-10 differentiation). MW-005 competes",

"description": "INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION chemistry with running-engine precondition: combustion is occurring but is inefficient due to mechanical sealing failure. Differentiated from non_starter family (which shares INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION chemistry) by the running-engine gate \u2014 OBD rpm > 600 as GATING (non_starter cases never reach running RPM). confidence_ceiling applied because INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION chemistry is shared with non_starter. v1 ERR-MW-001 reactivated with running-engine gate and non_starter competition awareness",

"description": "TIMING_RETARDED chemistry overlap \u2014 Tier B gap closer: low compression from mechanical wear causes late/incomplete combustion \u2192 TIMING_RETARDED chemistry as a secondary effect. Chemistry: TIMING_RETARDED as SUGGESTIVE evidence. Gated on DTC none_present for VVT_HISTORY range (P0010-P0025) \u2014 NO VVT DTCs may be present. This is the cam_timing differentiator: cam_timing TIMING_RETARDED cases carry VVT codes; mechanical_wear TIMING_RETARDED cases do not (the timing retardation is from sealing failure, not VVT malfunction). confidence_ceiling applied because TIMING_RETARDED chemistry is shared across 7 families. v1 had no equivalent rule (TIMING_RETARDED had zero v1 registrations)",

"description": "IGNITION_MISFIRE chemistry with mechanical-wear discriminators: GASLab classifies the combustion as misfire-type, but absence of P030x DTCs and depressed CO2 with low NOx point to mechanical sealing failure, not ignition. Differentiated from misfire by P0300-P0312 none_present DEFINITIVE, hc > 200 DEFINITIVE, and o2 < 4.0 GATING; the O2 gate excludes high-O2 no-DTC true misfire while preserving the CSV-120 mechanical-wear signature. FT-10",

"description": "Worn turbocharger turbine seals / oil consumption: oil leaks directly into the hot exhaust turbine housing, where it cracks post-cylinder in the hot exhaust. Combustion in-cylinder remains stoichiometric. Differentiated from PCV (MW-008) by stoichiometric lambda and low carbon monoxide, and from piston rings by the low-idle to high-idle HC drop.",
"description": "Classic ignition misfire from failed coil/plug/wire \u2014 high HC + high O2 with P0300-P0312 DTC confirmation",
"description": "Lean-induced misfire from vacuum leak or fuel starvation \u2014 lean chemistry with positive fuel trims and cylinder-fluid misfire evidence",
"description": "Rich misfire from injector leak or compression loss \u2014 rich chemistry with negative fuel trims",
"description": "Ghost misfire \u2014 ECU hallucinates P0300 from electrical noise, loose ground, or flywheel play despite pristine combustion chemistry",

"description": "ECU blindness \u2014 gas chemistry ground-truth shows misfire but ECU misfire counter reads zero; Brettschneider override: chemistry is truth, ECU counter is perception. IGNITION_MISFIRE is GATING (T-COMA-28, F-C1-2): no misfire chemistry, no ECU-blindness verdict",

"description": "Marginal-sample misfire with retarded timing \u2014 sample quality is borderline AND gas signature shows ignition-misfire-like chemistry with knock-avoidance timing pull; closes SAMPLE_INVALID and TIMING_RETARDED gaps for misfire family",
"description": "Clean stoichiometric no-DTC acceptance: low HC/CO, efficient CO2, low residual O2, moderate NOx, and lambda perception aligned with no confirmed DTCs",

"description": "LEAN_MISFIRE no-start: engine cranks but won't fire because insufficient or no fuel reaches the chamber. CO2 near-atmospheric (<5%) confirms no meaningful combustion occurred \u2014 the fuel either never arrived or never lit. Differentiated from misfire-family LEAN_MISFIRE by rpm < 600 and CO2 < 5% (running misfire cases have CO2 >= 10%). v1 had no equivalent LEAN_MISFIRE-gated rule for non_starter (ERR-NS-004 only gated on INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION)",

"description": "RICH_MISFIRE no-start (flooded): extreme cold enrichment floods the engine \u2014 fuel dumps into the chamber but won't light. CO2 near-atmospheric (<5%) confirms no meaningful combustion. ECT < 30 degC as SUGGESTIVE (REAL-003 is extreme cold enrichment). Differentiated from misfire-family RICH_MISFIRE by rpm < 600 and CO2 < 5% (running rich-misfire cases have CO2 >= 8% because some combustion IS occurring). v1 had no RICH_MISFIRE-gated rule for non_starter",

"description": "INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION no-start: partial/near-zero combustion yields incomplete combustion products. Chemistry-primary rule with rpm < 600 as GATING \u2014 this is the mechanical_wear differentiator (MW-005 gates on INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION with rpm > 600 GATING). The rpm gate creates a clean binary split: engine running \u2192 mechanical_wear; engine not running \u2192 non_starter. v1 ERR-NS-004 reactivated with the rpm GATING gate added (v1 had no OBD evidence and no cross-family competition awareness)",

"description": "DTC-driven fuel-delivery no-start: fuel pump circuit failure (P0230), low rail pressure (P0087), or rail pressure sensor fault (P0190) directly explains a no-start. DTC-primary rule \u2014 the DTC any_match is GATING, no chemistry gate. Chemistry LEAN_MISFIRE accepted as SUGGESTIVE (lean no-start is consistent with fuel starvation). base_weight 0.8 and confidence_ceiling 0.9 (T-COMA-3b): a DTC that names the failed component outranks the generic lean no-start NS-001 (ceiling 0.85), whose chemistry it shares. v1 had no equivalent DTC-driven non_starter rule",
